title.zh: 卷一百三十一 志第八十四 樂六
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 志第八十四 樂六 Volume 131 Treatises 84: Music 6

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，崇上壽皇聖帝、壽成皇后暨壽聖皇太后尊號，壽皇樂用《乾安》，壽聖、壽成樂用《坤安》，三殿慶禮，在當時侈為盛儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong received the abdication, he honored the Sovereign Father Emperor Shouhuang, Empress Shoucheng, and Empress Dowager Shousheng with honorific titles; for Shouhuang the music used was "Qian'an," for Shousheng and Shoucheng "Kun'an"; the celebratory rites of the three halls were at that time extravagantly accounted the grandest ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he bestowed honorific titles upon the Retired Emperor Shouhuang, Empress Shoucheng, and Empress Dowager Shousheng. "Qian'an" was played for Shouhuang, and "Kun'an" for Shousheng and Shoucheng. The celebration rites held in all three halls were regarded at the time as the most magnificent ceremonies ever staged.

sentences.zh: 尋以禮部、太常寺言：“國朝歲饗上帝，太祖肇造王業，則配冬饗於圜丘；

translations.literal: Soon the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "In our dynasty's yearly sacrifices to the Supreme Lord, Taizu, who first forged the royal enterprise, was paired at the winter sacrifice at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted a memorial: "In our dynasty's annual sacrifice to Heaven, Taizu, who founded the imperial enterprise, is associated at the winter offering at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 太宗混一區宇，則春祈穀、夏大雩、秋明堂俱配焉。

translations.literal: Taizong, who unified the realm, was paired at the spring grain prayer, summer great rain petition, and autumn Bright Hall alike.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, who unified the realm, is associated at the spring grain prayer, the summer great rain sacrifice, and the autumn Bright Hall ceremony alike.

sentences.zh: 高宗身濟大業，功德茂盛，所宜奉侑，仰繼祖宗，以協先儒嚴祖之議，以彰文祖配天之烈。”

translations.literal: Gaozong in person accomplished the great enterprise; his merit and virtue flourished—he ought to be honored as associated sacrifice, upholding the ancestors, to accord with the ancient scholars' discussion of revering the ancestral founder, to display the martial ancestor's glory of pairing with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong personally brought the great enterprise to completion, and his merit and virtue were abundant. He ought therefore to be received as an associated sacrifice, following the precedent of our forebears, in keeping with the ancient scholars' insistence on revering the founding ancestor, and to manifest the martial founder's glory in sharing Heaven's sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 乃季秋升侑於明堂，奠幣用《宗安之樂》，酌獻用《德安之樂》，並登歌作大呂宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon in late autumn he was elevated as associated sacrifice in the Bright Hall; presenting silks used the music "Zong'an," libation offering used "De'an," and ascension songs were composed in the great Lü palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in late autumn he was elevated as an associated sacrifice in the Bright Hall. "Zong'an" was used when presenting the silks, "De'an" for the libation offering, and the ascension songs were all composed in the palace mode of great Lü.

sentences.zh: 及加上高宗徽號，奉冊、寶以告，用《顯安之樂》。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong honorific title was added, presenting the register and seal to announce it used the music "Xian'an."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong's honorific title was conferred, the register and seal were presented in announcement with the music "Xian'an."

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，始行中宮冊禮，發冊於文德殿：皇帝升降御坐用《乾安之樂》，持節展禮官出入殿門用《正安之樂》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, the inner-palace investiture rite was first performed; the register was issued at Wende Hall: the emperor's ascending and descending the imperial seat used "Qian'an," officials bearing credentials performing the rite entering and leaving the hall gates used "Zheng'an."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi (1190), the inner-palace investiture ceremony was performed for the first time. The register was issued at Wende Hall: "Qian'an" accompanied the emperor's ascent and descent of the imperial seat, and "Zheng'an" when credential-bearing ritual officers entered and left the hall gates.

sentences.zh: 受冊於穆清殿：皇后出就褥位用《坤安》，至位用《承安》，受冊寶，用《成安》，受內外命婦賀就坐，用《和安》，內命婦進行賀禮，用《惠安》，外命婦進行賀禮用《鹹安》，皇后降坐用《徽安》，歸閣用《泰安》冊、寶入殿門用《宜安》。

translations.literal: The register was received at Muqing Hall: when the empress came out to the cushion position, "Kun'an"; arriving at position, "Cheng'an"; receiving the register and seal, "Cheng'an"; receiving congratulations from inner and outer titled ladies and taking her seat, "He'an"; inner titled ladies performing congratulations, "Hui'an"; outer titled ladies performing congratulations, "Xian'an"; the empress descending from her seat, "Hui'an"; returning to the pavilion, "Tai'an"; the register and seal entering the hall gates, "Yi'an."
translations.idiomatic: The register was received at Muqing Hall: "Kun'an" when the empress came out to the cushion seat, "Cheng'an" on reaching her position, "Cheng'an" when receiving the register and seal, "He'an" when she took her seat after receiving congratulations from titled ladies within and without the palace, "Hui'an" when inner titled ladies performed their congratulatory rites, "Xian'an" when outer titled ladies did the same, "Hui'an" when the empress descended, "Tai'an" on her return to the inner quarters, and "Yi'an" when the register and seal were brought through the hall gates.

sentences.zh: 宋初立後，自景祐始行冊命之禮。

translations.literal: When the Song first established empresses, from Jingyou onward the investiture appointment rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song, when an empress was first installed, the formal investiture ceremony was not performed until the Jingyou era (1034–1038).

sentences.zh: 元祐納後，典章彌盛，而六禮發制書日，樂備不作，惟皇后入宣德門，朝臣班迎，鳴鍾鼓而已。

translations.literal: When an empress was welcomed in the Yuanyou era, regulations grew ever more elaborate, yet on the day the six rites issued the imperial commission, though music was fully prepared it was not performed—only when the empress entered Xuande Gate did court officials array to welcome her, with bells and drums sounded, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanyou period (1086–1094), when an empress was welcomed, the ritual code had grown ever more elaborate; yet on the day the six rites issued the imperial commission, though the full musical apparatus was ready, no music was actually performed. Only when the empress entered Xuande Gate did the court officials form ranks to receive her, with bells and drums sounded—and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，乃陳宮架，用女工，皇后升降行止，並以樂為節。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era they arrayed the palace frame and used female performers; the empress's ascending, descending, walking, and stopping were all regulated by music.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era (1102–1106), the palace musical frame was arrayed and female performers employed; the empress's every ascent, descent, step, and pause was timed to the music.

sentences.zh: 至紹興復製樂，以重禕翟，詔執色勿用女工，令太常止於門外設樂。

translations.literal: By Shaoxing music was restored; to honor the sacred di headdress, an edict ordered that color-bearing performers not use female workers and commanded the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to set up music only outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shaoxing period (1131–1162) music was restored. To honor the sacred ceremonial headdress, an edict forbade female performers among the color-bearing musicians and directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to station the musicians outside the gate only.

sentences.zh: 隆興冊禮時，則國樂未舉，淳熙始遵用之，而紹熙敷賁舊典，於此特加詳備。

translations.literal: At the Longxing investiture rite state music had not yet been performed; in Chunxi it was first followed, and Shaoxi displayed the old canons, here adding particular fullness of detail.
translations.idiomatic: At the Longxing investiture (1163–1164) state music had not yet been performed; only in Chunxi (1174–1189) was it first adopted in full. Shaoxi then revived the old canon and added an especially detailed completeness to the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 紹興樂奏仲呂宮，仲呂為陰；

translations.literal: Shaoxing music was played in the zhonglü palace mode; zhonglü is yin;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing music was performed in the zhonglü palace mode, and zhonglü belongs to the yin register;

sentences.zh: 紹熙樂奏太簇宮，太簇為陽：用樂同而揆律異焉。

translations.literal: Shaoxi music was played in the taicu palace mode; taicu is yang: the music used was the same but the pitch standards differed.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxi music was performed in the taicu palace mode, and taicu belongs to the yang register: the pieces employed were the same, but the pitch standards differed.

sentences.zh: 明年郊祀，太常耿秉奏：“致敬鬼神，以禮樂為本，樂欲其備，音欲其和。

translations.literal: The next year at the suburban sacrifice, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Geng Bing memorialized: "Revering spirits and ghosts, ritual and music are the foundation; music should be complete, tones should be harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at the suburban sacrifice, Geng Bing of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "In paying homage to spirits and ghosts, ritual and music are the foundation. Music should be complete, and the tones harmonious.

sentences.zh: 今所用雷鼓之屬，正所以祀天致神，而皮革虛緩，聲不能振應；

translations.literal: The thunder drums and such now used are precisely for sacrificing to Heaven and summoning spirits, yet the leather is loose and slack, the sound cannot resonate in response;
translations.idiomatic: The thunder drums and their kind, now in use, are precisely what serve to sacrifice to Heaven and summon the spirits; yet their hides are slack and loose, and the sound cannot ring out in response;

sentences.zh: 登歌、大樂樂器及樂舞工人冠服，有積歲久而損弊者，宜葺新之。

translations.literal: The ascension songs, great music instruments, and music-dance workers' caps and robes—some worn for many years and damaged—should be repaired anew.
translations.idiomatic: The ascension-song instruments, the great ceremonial music apparatus, and the caps and robes of the musicians and dancers—some of which have deteriorated over many years—should be restored.

sentences.zh: 太常在籍樂工，不給於役，召募百姓，罕能習熟。

translations.literal: Musicians on the Court's register were insufficient for service; commoners were recruited, but few could learn thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The Court's registered musicians were too few to meet demand, and commoners recruited to fill the gap rarely mastered their parts.

sentences.zh: 郊祀事重，其樂工親扈乘輿，和樂雅奏，期以接天地、享祖宗，請優其日廩，以籍田司錢給之，樂藝稍精，仍加賞勸。

translations.literal: The suburban sacrifice is weighty; its musicians personally attend the imperial carriage, harmonizing elegant performance, expected to connect with Heaven and earth and honor the ancestors—please grant them superior daily provisions, supplied from the memorial-field office funds, so that musical skill may gradually improve, with rewards and encouragement added.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice is a weighty affair: its musicians attend the imperial carriage in person and perform the elegant harmonies, expected to link Heaven and earth and honor the ancestors. I beg that their daily provisions be increased, paid from the memorial-field office treasury, so that their skill may gradually improve, with rewards and encouragement added besides.

sentences.zh: 其緣托權要、送名充數者，嚴戢絕之。”

translations.literal: Those who relied on powerful connections to submit names merely to fill quotas should be strictly curtailed and cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Those who used connections with the powerful merely to submit names and fill quotas should be strictly suppressed and barred."

sentences.zh: 又言：“大禮前期，皇帝朝饗太廟，別廟內安穆、安恭皇后二室，前此係大臣分詣行事。

translations.literal: He also said: "Before the great rite, the emperor morning-sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; within the subsidiary temples were the two chambers of Empresses Anmu and Angong—previously high ministers went separately to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Before the great ceremony, the emperor performs the morning sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Within the subsidiary temples are the chambers of Empresses Anmu and Angong; previously high ministers went separately to conduct the rites.

sentences.zh: 今既親詣室祼，其酌獻、升殿所奏樂曲，恐不相協，宜命有司更製。”

translations.literal: Now that he personally goes to pour the libation at the chambers, the music played at libation offering and ascending the hall may not be harmoniously coordinated—it should be ordered that the responsible offices newly compose it."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he goes in person to pour the libation at the chambers, the music performed at the libation offering and the hall ascent may not be properly coordinated. The responsible offices should be ordered to compose new pieces."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was approved.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，孝宗升祔，祧僖祖，立別廟，禮官言：“僖祖既仿唐興聖立為別廟，遇祫則即廟以饗，孟冬祫饗日，合先詣僖祖廟室行禮。

translations.literal: When Ningzong took the throne, Xiaozong was elevated to the main line, Xizu was removed to a separate temple, and a separate temple was established. Ritual officers said: "Xizu, having been modeled on Tang's Xingsheng and established as a separate temple, when the collapse rite occurs sacrifices are performed at that temple; on the mid-winter collapse-sacrifice day, one should first go to the Xizu temple chamber to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Xiaozong was enshrined in the main temple line, Xizu was moved to a separate temple, and a dedicated shrine was established. The ritual officers submitted: "Xizu, having been established as a separate temple on the Tang model of Xingsheng, is sacrificed at his own shrine when the collapse rite is performed. On the mid-winter day of the collapse sacrifice, rites should first be conducted at Xizu's temple chamber.

sentences.zh: 其樂舞欲依每歲別廟五饗設樂禮例，於僖祖添設登歌樂。

translations.literal: The music and dance should follow the annual separate-temple five-sacrifice music rite precedent, adding ascension-song music for Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: The music and dance should follow the precedent for the five annual sacrifices at separate temples, with ascension-song music added for Xizu.

sentences.zh: 如僖廟行禮，就廟殿依次作登歌樂，其宮架樂則於太廟殿上通作。”

translations.literal: If performing rites at the Xi temple, perform ascension-song music in order at the temple hall; the palace-frame music is then performed throughout at the Imperial Ancestral Temple hall."
translations.idiomatic: When rites are performed at the Xi temple, the ascension songs should be played in sequence within the temple hall, while the palace-frame music is performed continuously in the main hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 既而臣僚言：“皇帝因重明聖節，詣壽康宮上壽舉樂，仰體聖主事親盡孝之誌，俯遂臣子尊君親上之忱，此國家典禮之大者也。

translations.literal: Then officials said: "Because the emperor on the Double Ninth holy day went to Shoukang Palace to offer longevity and perform music—upholding the sagely lord's utmost filial intent toward kin, below fulfilling subjects' reverence for ruler and parent—this is among the state's greatest ceremonial norms.
translations.idiomatic: Then the officials submitted: "On the Double Ninth holy day the emperor went to Shoukang Palace to offer longevity wishes and perform music—embodying the retired sovereign's utmost filial devotion to his parent, and fulfilling his subjects' reverence toward ruler and parent alike. This is among the greatest ceremonial norms of the state.

sentences.zh: 檢照典故，天申節賜禦筵，在上壽次日。

translations.literal: Checking precedents, on the Heavenly Application festival the imperial banquet was granted on the day after the longevity offering.
translations.idiomatic: According to precedent, on the Heavenly Application festival the imperial banquet was granted on the day following the longevity offering.

sentences.zh: 今乃於前一日賜文武百僚宴，重明上壽，用樂攸始，而臣下聽樂乃在君父之先，義有未安。”

translations.literal: Now on the day before, civil and military hundred officials were granted a feast; the Chongming longevity offering, with music thereby beginning, yet subjects heard music before ruler and father—there is impropriety in the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the feast for civil and military officials is granted on the day before. Music for the Chongming longevity offering has only just begun, while the subjects hear music before their ruler and father—this is improper in principle."

sentences.zh: 遂命改用次日。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was ordered to change to use the following day.
translations.idiomatic: The court accordingly ordered that the banquet be moved to the following day.

sentences.zh: 凡奉上冊寶於慈福、壽康宮者，再備樂行禮，一用乾道舊制。

translations.literal: Whenever presenting registers and seals to Cifu and Shoukang palaces, music and rites were again fully prepared, all using the Qiandao old system.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever registers and seals were presented to Cifu and Shoukang palaces, music and ceremonial rites were again fully provided, all according to the old Qiandao (1165–1173) regulations.

sentences.zh: 尋禦文德殿製冊皇后，有司請設宮架之樂，依儀施行。

translations.literal: Soon at Wende Hall the empress's register was composed; the responsible offices requested setting palace-frame music, performed according to the protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at Wende Hall, the empress's register was composed. The responsible offices requested the palace musical frame be set up and the ceremony performed according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年瑞慶節，金使至，以執光宗、慈懿皇后喪，詔就驛賜禦筵，並不作樂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan on the Auspicious Celebration festival, Jin envoys arrived; because they were observing mourning for Guangzong and Empress Ciyi, an edict granted the imperial banquet at the post station, with no music performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qingyuan (1200), on the Auspicious Celebration festival, Jin envoys arrived. Because the court was in mourning for Guangzong and Empress Ciyi, an edict directed that the imperial banquet be granted at the post station, with no music performed.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，明堂大饗，禮部尚書章穎奏：“太常工籍闕少，率差借執役。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading, at the Bright Hall great sacrifice, Minister of Rites Zhang Ying memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices registered craftsmen are short; they are mostly impressed for forced service.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiading (1209), at the Bright Hall great sacrifice, Zhang Ying, Minister of Rites, memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices has too few registered craftsmen and mostly impresses borrowed laborers for service.

sentences.zh: 當親行薦饗，或容不根遊手出入殿庭，非所以肅儀衛、嚴禁防也。

translations.literal: When personally performing the recommendation sacrifice, perhaps idlers not rooted in the craft may enter the hall court—not how to dignify protocol guards and tighten prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally performs the recommendation sacrifice, idle persons with no grounding in the craft may be allowed into the hall precincts—hardly the way to maintain dignified protocol and strict security.

sentences.zh: 乞申紹興、開禧已行禁令，不許用市井替名，顯示懲戒，庶俾駿奔之人小大嚴潔，以稱精禋。”

translations.literal: I beg to reissue the Shaoxing and Kaixi bans already enforced, not permitting marketplace substitutes by name, clearly showing punishment, so that those who hasten to serve may be great and small in strict purity, matching the refined sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the bans already enforced in Shaoxing and Kaixi be reissued, forbidding marketplace substitutes registered under false names, with punishments made visible, so that all who serve at the sacrifice, high and low alike, may be scrupulously proper and worthy of so refined a ceremony."

sentences.zh: 臣僚又奏：“郊祀登歌列於壇上，簉於上龕，蓋在天地祖宗之側也。

translations.literal: Officials also memorialized: "At suburban sacrifice the ascension songs are arrayed on the altar, beside the upper niche—they are beside Heaven and earth and the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The officials added: "At the suburban sacrifice the ascension songs are arrayed on the altar, beside the upper niche—they stand in the presence of Heaven and earth and the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 宮架列於午階下，則百神所同聽也。

translations.literal: The palace frame is arrayed below the noon steps, where all spirits equally listen.
translations.idiomatic: The palace frame is arrayed below the south steps, where all the spirits listen alike.

sentences.zh: 夫樂音莫尚於和，今絲、竹、管、弦類有闕斷，拊搏、佾舞，賤工、窶人往往垢玩猱雜，宜申嚴以肅祀事。”

translations.literal: Of musical sound nothing surpasses harmony; now silk, bamboo, pipe, and string types have breaks and gaps, clappers and dance performers—low workers and paupers often foul and mingle coarse play; it should be strictly enjoined to dignify sacrificial matters."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing in music surpasses harmony; yet now the silk, bamboo, pipe, and string instruments are broken and incomplete, and the clappers and dancers—often lowly workers and paupers—foul their instruments with careless handling. Strict enforcement is needed to dignify the sacrificial rites."

sentences.zh: 皆俞其請。

translations.literal: All approved their requests.
translations.idiomatic: All their requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，詔：“山東、河北連城慕義，殊俗郊順，奉玉寶來獻，其文曰‘皇帝恭膺天命之寶’，實惟我祖宗之舊。”

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year, an edict: "Shandong and Hebei linked cities admired righteousness; foreign customs submitted at the suburbs, presenting jade and treasure to offer. Its inscription read 'The Emperor Respectfully Receives Heaven's Mandate Treasure'—truly our ancestors' heirloom."
translations.idiomatic: By the fourteenth year (1222), an edict proclaimed: "Cities of Shandong and Hebei, moved by our righteousness, and foreign peoples submitting at the suburban sacrifice, have presented jade and treasure as tribute. The inscription reads 'The Emperor Respectfully Receives the Mandate of Heaven Treasure'—truly an heirloom of our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 乃明年元日，上御大慶殿受寶，用鼓吹導引，備陳宮架大樂，奏詩三章：一曰《恭膺天命》，二曰《舊疆來歸》，三曰《永清四海》，並奏以太簇宮。

translations.literal: Then on New Year's Day the next year, the emperor at Daqing Hall received the treasure, with drum-and-pipe escort, fully arraying palace-frame great music, performing three odes: first "Respectfully Receives Heaven's Mandate," second "Former Territories Return," third "Forever Clear the Four Seas," all performed in taicu palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: The following New Year's Day the emperor received the treasure at Daqing Hall, escorted by drums and pipes, with the full palace-frame great music arrayed. Three odes were performed: "Respectfully Receives Heaven's Mandate," "Former Territories Return," and "Forever Clear the Four Seas," all in the taicu palace mode.

sentences.zh: 理宗享國四十餘年，凡禮樂之事，式遵舊章，未嚐有所改作。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong enjoyed the state forty-odd years; all ritual and music matters followed old regulations, never altered or newly made.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong reigned for more than forty years; in all matters of ritual and music he followed the established regulations and never altered or newly composed anything.

sentences.zh: 先是，孝宗廟用《大倫之樂》，光宗廟用《大和之樂》；

translations.literal: Previously, the Xiaozong temple used "Dalun" music, the Guangzong temple "Dahe" music;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the Xiaozong temple used the music "Great Human Relations," and the Guangzong temple used "Great Harmony;"

sentences.zh: 至是，寧宗祔廟，用《大安之樂》。

translations.literal: At this time Ningzong was enshrined, using "Da'an" music.
translations.idiomatic: at this point, when Ningzong was enshrined, the music "Great Peace" was used.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年，行中宮冊禮，並用紹熙元年之典。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoding, the inner-palace investiture rite was performed, all using the Shaoxi first-year canon.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaoding (1230), the inner-palace investiture ceremony was performed, entirely according to the canon of Shaoxi's first year.

sentences.zh: 及奉上壽明仁福慈睿皇太后冊寶，始新製樂曲行事。

translations.literal: When presenting registers and seals to the longevity-honored Mingren Fuci Ruishou Empress Dowager, only then were new music pieces composed for the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Only when presenting the register and seal to Empress Dowager Shou Mingren Fuci Ruishou were new musical pieces composed for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 當時中興六七十載之間，士多歎樂典之久墜，類欲蒐講古製，以補遺軼。

translations.literal: At that time through sixty or seventy years of restoration, scholar-officials often lamented the long collapse of music canons, mostly wishing to gather and expound ancient systems to supply what was lost.
translations.idiomatic: During the sixty or seventy years of the restoration, scholar-officials frequently lamented how long the music canon had lain in ruins, and many wished to gather and expound ancient systems to restore what had been lost.

sentences.zh: 於是，薑夔乃進《大樂議》於朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiang Kui submitted the "Treatise on Great Music" to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jiang Kui presented his "Treatise on Great Music" to the court.

sentences.zh: 夔言：

translations.literal: Kui said:
translations.idiomatic: Kui wrote:

sentences.zh: 紹興大樂，多用大晟所造，有編鍾、鎛鍾、景鍾，有特磬、玉磬、編磬，三鍾三磬未必相應。

translations.literal: The Shaoxing great music largely used what Dasheng had made: there were serial bells, bo bells, and jing bells; there were special stone chimes, jade chimes, and serial stone chimes—the three bells and three chimes need not correspond.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaoxing great music relied largely on instruments made under the Dasheng Bureau. There were serial bells, bo bells, and jing bells; special stone chimes, jade chimes, and serial stone chimes—but the three bells and three chimes did not necessarily correspond with one another.

sentences.zh: 塤有大小，簫、篪、笛有長短，笙、竽之簧有厚薄，未必能合度，琴、瑟弦有緩急燥濕，軫有旋復，柱有進退，未必能合調。

translations.literal: Xun have large and small; xiao, chi, and di have long and short; sheng and yu's reeds have thick and thin—they need not match the standard measures. Qin and se strings have slack and tight, dry and wet; tuning pegs turn, bridges advance and retreat—they need not match tuning.
translations.idiomatic: The xun come in large and small sizes; the xiao, chi, and di in long and short; the reeds of the sheng and yu in thick and thin—they did not necessarily conform to the standard measures. The qin and se strings varied in tension, dryness, and moisture; the pegs turned and the bridges shifted—they did not necessarily achieve proper tuning.

sentences.zh: 總眾音而言之，金欲應石，石欲應絲，絲欲應竹，竹欲應匏，匏欲應土，而四金之音又欲應黃鍾，不知其果應否。

translations.literal: Taking all sounds together, metal should respond to stone, stone to silk, silk to bamboo, bamboo to gourd, gourd to earth—and the four metal tones should also respond to yellow bell; it is unknown whether they truly respond or not.
translations.idiomatic: Considering all the sounds together: metal should respond to stone, stone to silk, silk to bamboo, bamboo to gourd, gourd to earth—and the four metal tones should also respond to yellow bell. Whether they truly did so was unknown.

sentences.zh: 樂曲知以七律為一調，而未知度曲之義；

translations.literal: In musical pieces they knew to take the seven tones as one mode, but did not know the meaning of setting tunes;
translations.idiomatic: Composers knew to take the seven tones as one mode, but did not understand what it meant to set a tune properly;

sentences.zh: 知以一律配一字，而未知永言之旨。

translations.literal: they knew to match one tone to one character, but did not know the aim of sustained utterance.
translations.idiomatic: they knew to assign one tone to each character, but did not grasp the principle of sustained melodic phrasing.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾奏而聲或林鍾，林鍾奏而聲或太簇。

translations.literal: When yellow bell was played the sound might be forest bell; when forest bell was played the sound might be great cluster.
translations.idiomatic: When yellow bell was played, the sound produced might be forest bell; when forest bell was played, it might come out as great cluster.

sentences.zh: 七音之協四聲，各有自然之理。

translations.literal: The seven tones' coordination with the four tones each has its natural principle.
translations.idiomatic: The coordination of the seven tones with the four tones of Chinese phonology each follows a natural principle.

sentences.zh: 今以平、入配重濁，以上、去配輕清，奏之多不諧協。

translations.literal: Now level and entering tones are matched with heavy and thick, rising and departing with light and clear—when performed, much is not harmoniously coordinated.
translations.idiomatic: Now level and entering tones are paired with heavy, thick notes, and rising and departing tones with light, clear ones—yet in performance much of this coordination fails.

sentences.zh: 八音之中，琴、瑟尤難。

translations.literal: Among the eight sounds, qin and se are especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Among the eight categories of sound, the qin and se are especially difficult.

sentences.zh: 琴必每調而改弦，瑟必每調而退柱，上下相生，其理至妙，知之者鮮。

translations.literal: The qin must change strings for each mode, the se must withdraw bridges for each mode; upper and lower generate each other—the principle is most subtle, and few know it.
translations.idiomatic: The qin must have its strings changed for each mode, the se its bridges repositioned; upper and lower tones generate one another by a principle of utmost subtlety, and few understand it.

sentences.zh: 又琴、瑟聲微，常見蔽於鍾、磬、鼓、簫之聲；

translations.literal: Moreover, qin and se sounds are faint and are often obscured by the sounds of bells, chimes, drums, and xiao;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the qin and se are faint in sound and are often drowned out by bells, chimes, drums, and xiao;

sentences.zh: 匏、竹、土聲長，而金石常不能以相待，往往考擊失宜，消息未盡。

translations.literal: Gourd, bamboo, and earth sounds are long, while metal and stone often cannot wait upon each other; frequently the striking is improper and the resonance incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd, bamboo, and earth instruments sustain their tones, while metal and stone often cannot accommodate them; the striking is frequently mistimed and the resonance left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 至於歌詩，則一句而鍾四擊，一字而竽一吹，未協古人槁木貫珠之意。

translations.literal: As for sung poetry, one line brings four bell strikes, one character one yu breath—this does not accord with the ancients' meaning of dry wood strung with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: As for sung poetry, four bell strikes accompany a single line and one yu breath per character—far from the ancients' ideal of pearls strung on withered wood.

sentences.zh: 況樂工苟焉占籍，擊鍾磬者不知聲，吹匏竹者不知穴，操琴瑟者不知弦。

translations.literal: Moreover, musicians carelessly hold registry places: those who strike bells and chimes do not know sound, those who blow gourd and bamboo do not know holes, those who play qin and se do not know strings.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, musicians merely hold places on the registry: bell and chime players do not understand tone, gourd and bamboo players do not understand their instruments' holes, and qin and se players do not understand their strings.

sentences.zh: 同奏則動手不均，迭奏則發聲不屬。

translations.literal: When playing together their movements are uneven; when playing in alternation their sounds do not connect.
translations.idiomatic: When playing together their movements are uneven; when playing in alternation their sounds fail to connect.

sentences.zh: 比年人事不和，天時多忒，由大樂未有以格神人、召和氣也。

translations.literal: In recent years human affairs have been discordant and the seasons often errant—because great music has not yet been able to measure spirits and men and summon harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years human affairs have fallen into discord and the seasons have often gone awry—because great music has not yet been able to reach spirits and men and summon harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 宮為君、為父，商為臣、為子，宮商和則君臣父子和。

translations.literal: Gong is ruler and father, shang is minister and son; when gong and shang harmonize, ruler and minister, father and son harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Gong represents the ruler and the father, shang the minister and the son; when gong and shang are in harmony, ruler and minister, father and son are in harmony.

sentences.zh: 徵為火，羽為水，南方火之位，北方水之宅，常使水聲衰、火聲盛，則可助南而抑北。

translations.literal: Zhi is fire, yu is water; the south is fire's position, the north water's domain—constantly making water sound weak and fire sound strong can assist the south and restrain the north.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi is fire and yu is water; the south is fire's domain and the north water's home. By consistently weakening the water tone and strengthening the fire tone, one can support the south and restrain the north.

sentences.zh: 宮為夫，徵為婦，商雖父宮，實徵之子，常以婦助夫、子助母，而後聲成文。

translations.literal: Gong is husband, zhi is wife; though shang is gong's father, it is in fact zhi's son—constantly using wife to assist husband and son to assist mother, and only then does sound form pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Gong is the husband and zhi the wife; though shang is gong's parent tone, it is in fact zhi's child—by having the wife assist the husband and the son assist the mother, the tones then form a coherent pattern.

sentences.zh: 徵盛則宮唱而有和，商盛則徵有子而生生不窮，休祥不召而自至，災害不祓而自消。

translations.literal: When zhi flourishes, gong sings and has harmony; when shang flourishes, zhi has a son and generation upon generation is unending—auspicious omens arrive unbidden, disasters dissipate without exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: When zhi flourishes, gong leads the song and harmony follows; when shang flourishes, zhi has its child and generation succeeds generation without end. Auspicious omens arrive unbidden, and disasters dissipate without need of exorcism.

sentences.zh: 聖主方將講禮郊見，願詔求知音之士，考正太常之器，取所用樂曲，條理五音，隱括四聲，而使協和。

translations.literal: The sagely lord is about to expound ritual at the suburban audience; I wish an edict to seek those who know tones, examine and correct the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' instruments, take the music pieces used, arrange the five tones, encompass the four tones, and make them harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler is about to perform the suburban sacrifice and audience rites. I beg that an edict be issued to seek those who understand music, to examine and correct the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' instruments, to take the pieces now in use, arrange the five tones, encompass the four phonetic tones, and bring them into harmony.

sentences.zh: 然後品擇樂工，其上者教以金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、歌詩之事，其次者教以戛、擊、幹、羽、四金之事，其下不可教者汰之。

translations.literal: Then grade and select musicians: the highest teach metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, and sung poetry; the next teach striking, beating, shields, feathers, and the four metals; the lowest who cannot be taught, eliminate.
translations.idiomatic: Then grade and select the musicians: the best should be taught metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, and sung poetry; the next rank taught striking, beating, shields, feathers, and the four metal instruments; those at the bottom who cannot be taught should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 雖古樂未易遽復，而追還祖宗盛典，實在茲舉。

translations.literal: Though ancient music is not easily quickly restored, to pursue and return the ancestors' great ceremony truly lies in this undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Though ancient music cannot easily be restored at once, to recover the great ceremonies of our ancestors truly depends on this effort.

sentences.zh: 其議雅俗樂高下不一，宜正權衡度量：

translations.literal: His discussion: elegant and vulgar music's pitches are not uniform—weights, measures, and standards should be corrected:
translations.idiomatic: On the question that elegant and vulgar music differ in pitch and are not uniform, he argued that weights, measures, and pitch standards should be corrected:

sentences.zh: 自尺律之法亡於漢、魏，而十五等尺雜出於隋、唐正律之外，有所謂倍四之器，銀字、中管之號。

translations.literal: Since the foot-and-pitch standard method perished in Han and Wei, fifteen grades of foot measures miscellaneously emerged outside Sui and Tang proper pitch, with so-called double-four instruments and designations of silver character and middle pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the method of foot-and-pitch standards was lost in Han and Wei, fifteen grades of measuring foot emerged outside the proper pitch standards of Sui and Tang, along with so-called double-four instruments and designations such as silver character and middle pipe.

sentences.zh: 今大樂外有所謂下宮調，下宮調又有中管倍五者。

translations.literal: Now outside great music there is so-called lower palace mode; lower palace mode also has middle-pipe double-five.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the great ceremonial music there is now the so-called lower palace mode, and within lower palace mode there is also the middle-pipe double-five variant.

sentences.zh: 有曰羌笛、孤笛，曰雙韻、十四弦以意裁聲，不合正律，繁數悲哀，棄其本根，失之太清；

translations.literal: There are called Qiang flute and solitary flute, called double rhyme and fourteen strings—cutting sound by whim, not conforming to proper pitch, elaborate and mournful, abandoning their root, erring toward too clear;
translations.idiomatic: There are the Qiang flute and solitary flute, the double rhyme and fourteen-string instruments—shaping sound at whim, not conforming to proper pitch, elaborate and mournful, abandoning their musical roots, erring toward excessive clarity;

sentences.zh: 有曰夏笛、鷓鴣，曰胡盧琴、渤海琴，沉滯抑鬱。

translations.literal: There are called summer flute and partridge, called gourd lute and Bohai lute—heavy, stagnant, and depressed.
translations.idiomatic: There are the summer flute and partridge call, the gourd lute and Bohai lute—heavy, stagnant, and oppressive in tone.

sentences.zh: 腔調含糊，失之太濁。

translations.literal: Melodic patterns are indistinct, erring toward too thick.
translations.idiomatic: Their melodic patterns are indistinct, erring toward excessive thickness.

sentences.zh: 故聞其聲者，性情蕩於內，手足亂於外，《禮》所謂“慢易以犯節，流湎以忘本，廣則容奸，狹則思欲”者也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who hear their sounds have disordered natures within and chaotic hands and feet without—what the Rites calls "careless and easy in violating measure, flowing and drowning in forgetting the root; broad then harboring treachery, narrow then thinking of desire."
translations.idiomatic: Those who hear such sounds find their inner natures unsettled and their limbs in disorder—precisely what the Rites describes as "careless and easy in violating propriety, dissolute in forgetting one's roots; when broad, harboring treachery; when narrow, given to desire."

sentences.zh: 家自為權衡，鄉自為尺度，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Each household makes its own weights, each village its own measures—matters have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Each household sets its own weights, each village its own measures—and matters have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 謂宜在上明示以好惡。

translations.literal: He said the ruler above should clearly show likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the ruler above should make his preferences clearly known.

sentences.zh: 凡作樂製器者，一以太常所用及文思所頒為準。

translations.literal: All who make music and manufacture instruments should take solely what the Court of Imperial Sacrifices uses and what Wensi promulgates as standard.
translations.idiomatic: All who compose music and manufacture instruments should take as their sole standard what the Court of Imperial Sacrifices uses and what the Wensi Bureau promulgates.

sentences.zh: 其他私為高下多寡者悉禁之，則斯民“順帝之則”，而風俗可正。

translations.literal: All other private variations in pitch high and low or quantity should be forbidden; then this people will "follow the emperor's standard," and customs can be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: All other private variations in pitch or quantity should be forbidden; then the people will "follow the emperor's standard," and customs may be set right.

sentences.zh: 其議古樂止用十二宮：

translations.literal: His discussion: ancient music used only the twelve palace modes:
translations.idiomatic: On the question that ancient music used only the twelve palace modes, he argued:

sentences.zh: 周六樂奏六律、歌六呂，惟十二宮也。

translations.literal: Zhou's six great musics played the six lü and sang the six lü complement—only the twelve palace modes.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou six great ceremonial musics played the six lü and sang the six lü complement—nothing but the twelve palace modes.

sentences.zh: “王大食，三侑。”

translations.literal: "The king's great feasts, three libations."
translations.idiomatic: "The king's great feasts, with three libations."

sentences.zh: 注云：“朔日、月半。”

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The first day of the month and the month's midpoint."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: "The first day of the month and the month's midpoint."

sentences.zh: 隨月用律，亦十二宮也。

translations.literal: Following the month in using lü is also the twelve palace modes.
translations.idiomatic: Using the pitch standard appropriate to each month is likewise a matter of the twelve palace modes.

sentences.zh: 十二管各備五聲，合六十聲；

translations.literal: The twelve pipes each equipped with five sounds, totaling sixty sounds;
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pipes each carry the five tones, making sixty tones in all;

sentences.zh: 五聲成一調，故十二調。

translations.literal: five sounds forming one mode, hence twelve modes.
translations.idiomatic: five tones forming one mode, hence twelve modes.

sentences.zh: 古人於十二宮又特重黃鍾一宮而已。

translations.literal: The ancients among the twelve palace modes especially valued only the yellow bell palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Among the twelve palace modes, the ancients especially valued only the yellow bell mode.

sentences.zh: 齊景公作《徵招》、《角招》之樂，師涓、師曠有清商、清角、清徵之操。

translations.literal: Duke Jing of Qi composed the music "Zhi Summons" and "Jue Summons"; Shi Juan and Shi Kuang had the pieces Clear Shang, Clear Jue, and Clear Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing of Qi composed "Zhi Summons" and "Jue Summons"; the masters Shi Juan and Shi Kuang had pieces in Clear Shang, Clear Jue, and Clear Zhi.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，燕樂或用之，雅樂未聞有以商、角、徵、羽為調者，惟迎氣有五引而已，《隋書》雲“梁、陳雅樂，並用宮聲”是也。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward, banquet music sometimes used them; elegant music has not been heard to take shang, jue, zhi, or yu as modes—only welcoming qi had the five introductions; the Book of Sui says "Liang and Chen elegant music both used gong tone"—that is so.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, banquet music sometimes employed them, but elegant music was never known to use shang, jue, zhi, or yu as modes—only the five introductions for welcoming the seasons. The Book of Sui states that "Liang and Chen elegant music both used the gong tone," and this is correct.

sentences.zh: 若鄭譯之八十四調，出於蘇祗婆之琵琶。

translations.literal: As for Zheng Yi's eighty-four modes, they came from Su Zhiba's pipa.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi's eighty-four modes, for instance, derived from Su Zhiba's pipa.

sentences.zh: 大食、小食、般涉者，胡語；

translations.literal: Dashi, xiaoshi, and banshe are barbarian terms;
translations.idiomatic: Dashi, xiaoshi, and banshe are foreign terms;

sentences.zh: 《伊州》、《石州》、《甘州》、《婆羅門》者，胡曲；

translations.literal: "Yizhou," "Shizhou," "Ganzhou," and "Brahmana" are barbarian tunes;
translations.idiomatic: "Yizhou," "Shizhou," "Ganzhou," and "Brahmana" are foreign melodies;

sentences.zh: 《綠腰》、《誕黃龍》、《新水調》者，華聲而用胡樂之節奏。

translations.literal: "Green Waist," "Birth of the Yellow Dragon," and "New Water Mode" are Chinese sounds using barbarian music's rhythms.
translations.idiomatic: "Green Waist," "Birth of the Yellow Dragon," and "New Water Mode" are Chinese melodies set to foreign rhythmic patterns.

sentences.zh: 惟《瀛府》、《獻仙音》謂之法曲，即唐之法部也。

translations.literal: Only "Yingfu" and "Offering Immortal Music" are called fayue (courtly pieces)—that is, the Tang dynasty's fayue department.
translations.idiomatic: Only the pieces "Yingfu" and "Offering Immortal Music" are termed courtly pieces (fayue); these are the Tang dynasty's courtly music department.

sentences.zh: 凡有催袞者，皆胡曲耳，法曲無是也。

translations.literal: All that have accelerated ornament (cuigun) are Hu tunes; fayue has none of this.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever pieces employ accelerated ornamentation are foreign tunes; courtly pieces have no such feature.

sentences.zh: 且其名八十四調者，其實則有黃鍾、太簇、夾鍾、仲呂、林鍾、夷則、無射七律之宮、商、羽而已，於其中又闕太簇之商、羽焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, though they are named the eighty-four modes, in reality there are only the gong, shang, and yu of the seven tones Huangzhong, Taicu, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Yize, and Wushe—and among these the shang and yu of Taicu are still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, although they are called the eighty-four modes, in practice there are only the gong, shang, and yu modes for the seven tones Huangzhong, Taicu, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Yize, and Wushe—and even among these, the shang and yu of Taicu are missing.

sentences.zh: 國朝大樂諸曲，多襲唐舊。

translations.literal: The great music pieces of our dynasty mostly follow Tang precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the great ceremonial music pieces of our dynasty largely follow Tang models.

sentences.zh: 竊謂以十二宮為雅樂，周製可舉；

translations.literal: I venture to say that taking the twelve gong modes as elegant music, the Zhou system can be adopted;
translations.idiomatic: I would suggest that the twelve gong modes be adopted as elegant music, following the Zhou system;

sentences.zh: 以八十四調為宴樂，胡部不可雜。

translations.literal: taking the eighty-four modes as banquet music—the Hu department must not be mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: and that the eighty-four modes serve as banquet music, without mixing in foreign music.

sentences.zh: 郊廟用樂，鹹當以宮為曲，其間皇帝升降、盥洗之類，用黃鍾者，群臣以太簇易之，此周人王用《王夏》、公用《驁夏》之義也。

translations.literal: For suburban and temple music, all should take gong as the mode for pieces; among these, where the emperor's ascent and descent or ablutions use Huangzhong, the ministers replace it with Taicu—this is the meaning of the Zhou people's king using "Royal Summer" and duke using "Piebald Summer."
translations.idiomatic: For suburban and temple rites, all music should be set in the gong mode; where the emperor's ascent, descent, or ablutions would use Huangzhong, the ministers substitute Taicu—just as in Zhou times the king performed to "Royal Summer" and a duke to "Piebald Summer."

sentences.zh: 其議登歌當與奏樂相合：

translations.literal: His proposal: ascending song should match the performed music:
translations.idiomatic: His proposal on ascending song and instrumental performance:

sentences.zh: 《周官》歌奏，取陰陽相合之義。

translations.literal: In the "Offices of Zhou," song and performance take the meaning of yin and yang harmonizing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Offices of Zhou, singing and instrumental performance embody the principle of yin and yang in harmony.

sentences.zh: 歌者，登歌、徹歌是也；

translations.literal: "Song" means ascending song and withdrawal song;
translations.idiomatic: "Song" refers to ascending song and withdrawal song;

sentences.zh: 奏者，金奏、下管是也。

translations.literal: "Performance" means metal performance and lower pipes.
translations.idiomatic: "Performance" refers to metal percussion and lower wind instruments.

sentences.zh: 奏六律主乎陽，歌六呂主乎陰，聲不同而德相合也，自唐以來始失之。

translations.literal: Performing the six lü is yang-dominant; singing the six lü is yin-dominant—the sounds differ yet their virtue harmonizes; since the Tang this has first been lost.
translations.idiomatic: The six lü in performance are yang-dominant; the six lü in song are yin-dominant—the timbres differ yet their virtue harmonizes. This principle has been lost since the Tang.

sentences.zh: 故趙慎言云：祭祀有下奏太簇、上歌黃鍾，俱是陽律，既違禮經，抑乖會合。”

translations.literal: Therefore Zhao Shenyan said: in sacrifice there is lower performance of Taicu and upper song of Huangzhong—both are yang modes, violating the ritual classics and also contrary to harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zhao Shenyan remarked: in sacrifice, performing Taicu below while singing Huangzhong above—both yang modes—violates the ritual classics and defeats their intended harmony."

sentences.zh: 今太常樂曲，奏夾鍾者奏陰歌陽，其合宜歌無射，乃或歌大呂；

translations.literal: Now in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' music pieces: where Jiazhong is performed, yin is performed and yang is sung—the proper match should sing Wushe, yet sometimes they sing Dalü;
translations.idiomatic: In the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' repertoire today: where Jiazhong is performed (yin), yang is sung—the proper pairing should be Wushe, yet sometimes Dalü is sung instead;

sentences.zh: 奏函鍾者奏陰歌陽，其合宜歌蕤賓，乃或歌應鍾；

translations.literal: where Hanzhong is performed, yin is performed and yang is sung—the proper match should sing Ruibin, yet sometimes they sing Yingzhong;
translations.idiomatic: where Hanzhong is performed (yin), yang is sung—the proper pairing should be Ruibin, yet sometimes Yingzhong is sung;

sentences.zh: 奏黃鍾者奏陽歌陰，其合宜歌大呂，乃雜歌夷則、夾鍾、仲呂、無射矣。

translations.literal: where Huangzhong is performed, yang is performed and yin is sung—the proper match should sing Dalü, yet they mix in singing Yize, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, and Wushe.
translations.idiomatic: where Huangzhong is performed (yang), yin should be sung—the proper pairing is Dalü, yet Yize, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, and Wushe are sung indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 苟欲合天人之和，此所當改。

translations.literal: If one wishes to harmonize Heaven and man, this is what must be changed.
translations.idiomatic: If one seeks harmony between Heaven and humanity, these are the points that must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 其議祀享惟登歌、徹豆當歌詩：

translations.literal: His proposal: in sacrificial offerings, only ascending song and bean withdrawal should sing odes:
translations.idiomatic: His proposal on sacrificial music and when to sing odes:

sentences.zh: 古之樂，或奏以金，或吹以管，或吹以笙，不必皆歌詩。

translations.literal: Ancient music sometimes was performed with metal, sometimes blown on pipes, sometimes blown on sheng—not necessarily all singing odes.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient music, pieces were sometimes performed on metal percussion, sometimes on pipes, sometimes on the sheng—not every piece required singing an ode.

sentences.zh: 周有《九夏》，鍾師以鍾鼓奏之，此所謂奏以金也。

translations.literal: The Zhou had the "Nine Summers"; the bell master performed them with bells and drums—this is what is called performing with metal.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had the Nine Summers, performed by the bell master on bells and drums—this is what is meant by performing with metal.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀登歌既畢，下管《象》、《武》。

translations.literal: After the great sacrifice's ascending song was finished, the lower pipes performed "Xiang" and "Wu."
translations.idiomatic: After the ascending song of a great sacrifice concluded, the lower pipes performed "Xiang" and "Wu."

sentences.zh: 管者，簫、篪、笛之屬。

translations.literal: Pipes are the xiao, chi, and di and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes comprise the xiao, chi, di, and related instruments.

sentences.zh: 《象》、《武》皆詩而吹其聲，此所謂吹以管者也。

translations.literal: "Xiang" and "Wu" are both odes yet their sounds are blown—this is what is called blowing on pipes.
translations.idiomatic: "Xiang" and "Wu" are odes whose melodies were blown on pipes—this is what is meant by blowing on pipes.

sentences.zh: 周六笙詩，自《南陔》皆有聲而無其詩，笙師掌之以供祀饗，此所謂吹以笙者也。

translations.literal: The Zhou's six sheng odes, from "Southern Hills" onward, all had sound but no ode text; the sheng master managed them to supply sacrificial feasts—this is what is called blowing on sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou's six sheng pieces, from "Southern Hills" onward, had melodies but no surviving texts; the sheng master performed them for sacrifices and feasts—this is what is meant by blowing on the sheng.

sentences.zh: 周升歌《清廟》，徹而歌《雍》詩，一大祀惟兩歌詩。

translations.literal: The Zhou's ascending song was "Clear Temple"; at withdrawal they sang the "Yong" ode—a great sacrifice had only two sung odes.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ascended with "Clear Temple" and withdrew singing "Yong"—a great sacrifice employed only two sung odes.

sentences.zh: 漢初，此製未改，迎神曰《嘉至》，皇帝入曰《永至》：皆有聲無詩。

translations.literal: In early Han this system was not yet changed: welcoming the spirit was called "Fine Arrival," the emperor's entrance was called "Eternal Arrival"—both had sound but no ode.
translations.idiomatic: In early Han this system remained: welcoming the spirit used "Fine Arrival," the emperor's entrance used "Eternal Arrival"—both had melodies but no texts.

sentences.zh: 至晉始失古製，既登歌有詩，夕牲有詩，饗神有詩，迎神、送神又有詩。

translations.literal: By the Jin the ancient system was first lost: ascending song had odes, evening sacrifice had odes, feasting the spirit had odes, welcoming and sending the spirit also had odes.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jin the ancient system was lost: ascending song, evening sacrifice, spirit feasting, and welcoming and sending the spirit—all had sung odes.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐至今，詩歌愈富，樂無虛作。

translations.literal: From Sui and Tang to the present, odes grow ever richer; music has no idle composition.
translations.idiomatic: From Sui and Tang to the present, sung odes have proliferated until no musical moment lacks a text.

sentences.zh: 謂宜仿周製，除登歌、徹歌外，繁文當刪，以合於古。

translations.literal: He said it is fitting to imitate the Zhou system: apart from ascending song and withdrawal song, redundant texts should be cut to accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed imitating the Zhou system: apart from ascending and withdrawal songs, superfluous texts should be removed to restore ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 其議作鼓吹曲以歌祖宗功德：

translations.literal: His proposal: compose drum-and-blow pieces to sing the ancestors' merit and virtue:
translations.idiomatic: His proposal on composing drum-and-blow pieces to celebrate ancestral merit:

sentences.zh: 古者，祖宗有功德，必有詩歌，《七月》之陳王業是也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when ancestors had merit and virtue, there were necessarily odes—"Seventh Month" presenting the king's enterprise is such.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when ancestors achieved merit and virtue, odes inevitably followed—"Seventh Month," presenting the royal enterprise, is an example.

sentences.zh: 歌於軍中，周之愷樂、愷歌是也。

translations.literal: Singing in the army—the Zhou's triumphant music and triumphant song are such.
translations.idiomatic: Singing in the army—the Zhou's triumphant music and songs are examples.

sentences.zh: 漢有短簫鐃歌之曲凡二十二篇，軍中謂之騎吹，其曲曰《戰城南》、《聖人出》之類是也。

translations.literal: The Han had short xiao and nao song pieces totaling twenty-two, called in the army cavalry blow; their pieces such as "Battle South of the City" and "The Sage Appears" are such.
translations.idiomatic: The Han possessed twenty-two short xiao and nao song pieces, termed cavalry blow in the army—pieces such as "Battle South of the City" and "The Sage Appears."

sentences.zh: 魏因其聲，製為《克官渡》等曲十有二篇；

translations.literal: Wei took their sounds and made pieces such as "Conquering Guandu" totaling twelve;
translations.idiomatic: Wei adapted these melodies into twelve pieces, including "Conquering Guandu";

sentences.zh: 晉亦製為《征遼東》等曲二十篇；

translations.literal: Jin also made pieces such as "Campaigning in Liaodong" totaling twenty;
translations.idiomatic: Jin likewise composed twenty pieces, including "Campaigning in Liaodong";

sentences.zh: 唐柳宗元亦嚐作為鐃歌十有二篇，述高祖、太宗功烈。

translations.literal: Tang's Liu Zongyuan also once composed twelve nao songs narrating Gaozu and Taizong's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Liu Zongyuan likewise once composed twelve nao songs recounting the achievements of Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 我朝太祖、太宗平僭偽，一區宇；

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Taizu and Taizong pacified usurpers and false regimes, unifying the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's Taizu and Taizong suppressed usurpers and reunified the realm;

sentences.zh: 真宗一戎衣而卻契丹；

translations.literal: Zhenzong with one suit of armor repelled the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong repelled the Khitan at a single stroke;

sentences.zh: 仁宗海涵春育，德如堯、舜；

translations.literal: Renzong embraced all like the sea and nourished like spring, his virtue like Yao and Shun;
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's virtue encompassed all as the sea and nourished as spring, rivaling Yao and Shun;

sentences.zh: 高宗再造大功，上儷祖宗。

translations.literal: Gaozong recreated great merit, matching the ancestors above.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong restored the dynasty in grand achievement, equaling his forebears.

sentences.zh: 願詔文學之臣，追述功業之盛，作為歌詩，使知樂者協以音律，領之太常，以播於天下。

translations.literal: May it be decreed that literary officials trace and narrate the splendor of these achievements, compose them as songs and odes, have those who understand music harmonize them to pitch standards, and have the Court of Imperial Sacrifices lead them to broadcast throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: May literary officials be commissioned to recount these splendid achievements in song and ode, have musicians set them to proper pitch, and entrust the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to disseminate them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 夔乃自作《聖宋鐃歌曲》：宋受命曰《上帝命》，平上黨曰《河之表》，定維揚曰《淮海濁》，取湖南曰《沅之上》，得荊州曰《皇威暢》，取蜀曰《蜀山邃》，取廣南曰《時雨霈》，下江南曰《望鍾山》，吳越獻國曰《大哉仁》，漳、泉獻土曰《謳歌歸》，克河東曰《伐功繼》，征澶淵曰《帝臨墉》，美仁治曰《維四葉》，歌中興曰《炎精復》，凡十有四篇，上於尚書省。

translations.literal: Kui then himself composed the "Holy Song Nao Songs": Song receiving the Mandate was called "Heaven's Command," pacifying Shangdang was called "Beyond the River," securing Weiyang was called "Huaihai Turbid," taking Hunan was called "Above the Yuan," obtaining Jingzhou was called "Imperial Might Unfettered," taking Shu was called "Shu Mountains Deep," taking Guangnan was called "Seasonal Rain Abundant," subduing Jiangnan was called "Gazing at Zhong Mountain," Wu and Yue submitting their states was called "How Great the Benevolence," Zhang and Quan offering territory was called "Songs of Praise Return," conquering Hedong was called "Merit of Campaign Continued," campaigning at Chanyuan was called "The Emperor Approaches the Rampart," praising benevolent governance was called "Sustaining Four Generations," singing the restoration was called "Blazing Essence Restored"—fourteen pieces in all, submitted to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kui then composed the "Holy Song Nao Songs" himself: "Heaven's Command" for the Song receiving the Mandate, "Beyond the River" for pacifying Shangdang, "Huaihai Turbid" for securing Weiyang, "Above the Yuan" for taking Hunan, "Imperial Might Unfettered" for obtaining Jingzhou, "Shu Mountains Deep" for conquering Shu, "Seasonal Rain Abundant" for taking Guangnan, "Gazing at Zhong Mountain" for subduing Jiangnan, "How Great the Benevolence" for Wu and Yue's submission, "Songs of Praise Return" for Zhang and Quan's offering of territory, "Merit of Campaign Continued" for conquering Hedong, "The Emperor Approaches the Rampart" for the Chanyuan campaign, "Sustaining Four Generations" praising benevolent rule, and "Blazing Essence Restored" celebrating the restoration—fourteen pieces in all, submitted to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔付太常。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; an edict handed it to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict entrusted it to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 然夔言為樂必定黃鍾，迄無成說。

translations.literal: Yet Kui said that establishing music must fix Huangzhong—to the end no settled theory was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kui insisted that establishing music required fixing Huangzhong as the standard—and no settled theory was ever reached.

sentences.zh: 其議今之樂極為詳明，而終謂古樂難復，則於樂律之原有未及講。

translations.literal: His discussions of present music were extremely detailed and clear, yet in the end he said ancient music was hard to restore—thus the origins of pitch standards were not fully expounded.
translations.idiomatic: His analysis of contemporary music was remarkably thorough, yet he ultimately held that ancient music could not be restored—leaving the origins of pitch standards insufficiently explored.

sentences.zh: 其後，朱熹深悼先王製作之湮泯，與其友武夷蔡元定相與講明，反覆參訂，以究其歸極。

translations.literal: Afterward, Zhu Xi deeply lamented the obliteration of the former kings' creations; with his friend Wuyi's Cai Yuanding he mutually expounded and clarified, repeatedly collating and revising, to investigate their ultimate principles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhu Xi deeply lamented the obliteration of the former kings' musical creations. With his friend Cai Yuanding of Wuyi he engaged in sustained study, repeatedly collating and revising their work to reach its fundamental principles.

sentences.zh: 熹在慶元經筵，嚐草奏曰：“自秦滅學，禮樂先壞，而樂之為教，絕無師授。

translations.literal: Xi, at the Qingyuan Classics Lectures, once drafted a memorial saying: "Since Qin extinguished learning, ritual and music were first ruined, and music as instruction has utterly lacked teacher transmission.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qingyuan Classics Lectures, Xi once drafted a memorial stating: "Since the Qin extinguished learning, ritual and music were the first to collapse, and music as a discipline has lacked any transmission from masters.

sentences.zh: 律尺短長，聲音清濁，學士大夫莫知其說，而不知其為闕也。

translations.literal: The pitch standard's measure short and long, sound clear and murky—scholar-officials know none of its explanations, and do not know it is a lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: The length of pitch measures, the clarity and murkiness of tones—scholar-officials know nothing of these matters, unaware even that this constitutes a grave deficiency.

sentences.zh: 望明詔許臣招致學徒，聚禮樂諸書，編輯別為一書，以補六藝之闕。”

translations.literal: I hope for a clear edict permitting your servant to summon students, gather ritual and music books, compile and separately make one book, to supplement the Six Arts' lacuna."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request a clear edict permitting me to gather students, collect works on ritual and music, and compile them into a separate volume to fill the gap in the Six Arts."

sentences.zh: 後修禮書，定為《鍾律》、《樂製》等篇，垂憲言以貽後人。

translations.literal: Later, revising the Book of Rites, he fixed chapters such as "Bell Standards" and "Music Institutions," leaving constitutional words to bequeath to later people.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while compiling his Book of Rites, he established chapters on "Bell Standards" and "Music Institutions," leaving authoritative teachings for posterity.

sentences.zh: 蓋宋之樂議，因時迭出，其樂律高下不齊，俱有原委。

translations.literal: Broadly, the Song's music discussions emerged in succession with the times; their pitch standards' high and low were not uniform—all had origins and developments.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Song debates on music emerged successively over time; their pitch standards varied in height, each with its own history and rationale.

sentences.zh: 建隆初用王樸樂，藝祖一聽，嫌其太高，近於哀思，詔和峴考西京表尺，令下一律，比舊樂始和暢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong they used Wang Pu's music; the Founding Emperor upon one hearing disliked it as too high, near to mournful thought; he decreed He Ning examine the Western Capital's pitch measure, ordering one pitch lowered—compared to old music it first became harmonious and smooth.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianlong, Wang Pu's music was adopted. The Founding Emperor, upon hearing it once, found it too high and uncomfortably mournful. He ordered He Ning to examine the Western Capital pitch measure and lower the pitch by one degree; compared with the previous music, it first became harmonious.

sentences.zh: 至景祐、皇祐間，訪樂、議樂之詔屢頒，於是命李照改定雅樂，比樸下三律。

translations.literal: By the Jingyou and Huangyou periods, edicts seeking and debating music were repeatedly issued; thereupon Li Zhao was ordered to revise elegant music, three pitches lower than Pu.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingyou and Huangyou reigns, edicts commissioning music research and debate were issued repeatedly. Li Zhao was then ordered to revise elegant music, three pitches lower than Pu's standard.

sentences.zh: 照以縱黍累尺，雖律應古樂，而所造鍾磬，才中太簇，樂與器自相矛盾。

translations.literal: Zhao used stacking millet to accumulate the foot; though the pitch standards accorded with ancient music, the bells and chime stones he made only matched Taicu—music and instruments contradicted each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao used the method of stacking millet grains to determine the foot. Although his pitch standards accorded with ancient music in theory, the bells and chime stones he cast only matched Taicu—music and instruments contradicted one another.

sentences.zh: 阮逸、胡瑗復定議，止下一律，以尺生律，而黃鍾律短，所奏樂聲復高。

translations.literal: Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan again fixed the discussion, lowering only one pitch, generating pitch standards from the foot—but the Huangzhong standard was short, and the performed music's sound was again high.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan revised the standard again, lowering only one pitch and deriving pitch standards from the foot measure—but the Huangzhong standard proved too short, and the performed music sounded high once more.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，以楊傑條樂之疵，召範鎮、劉幾參定。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng period, because Yang Jie itemized music's defects, Fan Zhen and Liu Ji were summoned to participate in fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng reign, Yang Jie enumerated defects in the music system, and Fan Zhen and Liu Ji were summoned to assist in revising it.

sentences.zh: 幾、傑所奏，下舊樂三律，範鎮以為聲雜鄭、衛，且律有四厘六毫之差，太簇為黃鍾，宮商易位，欲求真黍以正尺律，造樂來獻，復下李照一律。

translations.literal: What Ji and Jie submitted lowered old music by three pitches; Fan Zhen held the sound mixed with Zheng and Wei music, and moreover the pitch standards had a discrepancy of four li and six hao—Taicu became Huangzhong, gong and shang exchanged positions; wishing to seek true millet to correct foot and pitch standards, he made music and came to present it, yet it was again lowered one pitch from Li Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Jie proposed lowering the old music by three pitches. Fan Zhen objected that the sound resembled vulgar Zheng and Wei music, and that the pitch standards were off by four li and six hao—Taicu was mistaken for Huangzhong, gong and shang reversed. Seeking true millet to correct the foot and pitch measures, he composed new music and presented it, yet the court lowered it one pitch from Li Zhao's standard.

sentences.zh: 至元祐廷奏，而詔獎之。

translations.literal: By the Yuanyou court performance, an edict commended it.
translations.idiomatic: When it was performed at court during Yuanyou, an edict commended the achievement.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮以房庶所得《漢書》，其言黍律異於他本，以大府尺為黃帝時尺，司馬光力辨其不然。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhen relied on Fang Shu's obtained Book of Han, whose words on millet and pitch standards differed from other versions, taking the Grand Storehouse foot as the Yellow Emperor's foot—Sima Guang forcefully argued this was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Fan Zhen relied on a Book of Han obtained by Fang Shu, whose account of millet and pitch standards differed from other versions, and took the Grand Storehouse foot as the Yellow Emperor's measure—Sima Guang vigorously disputed this.

sentences.zh: 鎮以周鬴、漢斛為據，光謂鬴本《考工》所記，斛本劉歆所作，非經不足法。

translations.literal: Zhen took the Zhou cauldron and Han hu as evidence; Guang said the cauldron was originally recorded in the "Artificers' Standards," the hu originally made by Liu Xin—not classics, insufficient to take as law.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen cited the Zhou cauldron and Han hu as evidence. Guang replied that the cauldron was recorded only in the Artificers' Standards and the hu was devised by Liu Xin—neither being canonical texts, neither could serve as authoritative precedent.

sentences.zh: 鎮以所收開元中笛及方響合於仲呂，校太常樂下五律，教坊樂下三律。

translations.literal: Zhen took his collected Kaiyuan-period flute and square sounding stone as matching Zhonglü, adjusting the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' music down five pitches and the Music Bureau's music down three.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen argued that a Kaiyuan-period flute and square sounding stone in his collection matched Zhonglü, and proposed lowering the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' music by five pitches and the Music Bureau's by three.

sentences.zh: 光謂此特開元之仲呂，未必合於後夔，力止鎮勿奏所為樂。

translations.literal: Guang said this was merely Kaiyuan's Zhonglü, not necessarily matching Hou Kui; he forcefully stopped Zhen from performing the music he had made.
translations.idiomatic: Guang countered that this was merely the Kaiyuan period's Zhonglü, not necessarily matching Hou Kui's standard, and vigorously prevented Fan Zhen from presenting his newly composed music.

sentences.zh: 光與鎮平生大節不謀而同，惟鍾律之論往返爭議，凡三十餘年，終不能以相一。

translations.literal: Guang and Zhen in life shared great integrity without planning yet alike—only in bell-standard discussions they disputed back and forth for over thirty years, to the end unable to make each other agree.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and Fan Zhen shared the same moral integrity throughout their lives, yet on bell standards they debated back and forth for over thirty years without ever reaching agreement.

sentences.zh: 是時，濂、洛、關輔諸儒繼起，遠溯聖傳，義理精究。

translations.literal: At this time, the Lian, Luo, and Guanfu region scholars arose in succession, tracing far back to the sage transmission, exhaustively investigating principle and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, scholars of the Lian, Luo, and Guanfu traditions arose in succession, tracing the sage transmission to its roots and pursuing principle with rigorous precision.

sentences.zh: 周惇頤之言樂，有曰：“古者聖王製禮法、修教化，三綱正，九疇敘，百姓大和，萬物鹹若，乃作樂以宣八風之氣。

translations.literal: Zhou Dunyi's words on music say: "In antiquity the sage kings made ritual law and cultivated transformation; the three bonds were rectified, the nine categories ordered, the hundred surnames greatly harmonized, the ten thousand things all compliant—then they made music to disseminate the eight winds' qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dunyi wrote on music: "In antiquity the sage kings established ritual law and cultivated moral transformation. When the three bonds were rectified and the nine categories ordered, when the people lived in great harmony and all things flourished, they then composed music to disseminate the qi of the eight winds.

sentences.zh: 樂聲淡而不傷，和而不淫。

translations.literal: Music's sound is plain yet not injurious, harmonious yet not licentious.
translations.idiomatic: Its sound was plain yet not harsh, harmonious yet not licentious.

sentences.zh: 淡則欲心平，和則躁心釋。

translations.literal: Plainness then levels the desire-mind; harmony then releases the restless mind.
translations.idiomatic: Plainness calmed the mind of desire; harmony released the restless mind.

sentences.zh: 德盛治至，道配天地，古之極也。

translations.literal: Virtue flourishing and governance arriving, the Way matching Heaven and Earth—antiquity's utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue flourished and governance reached perfection, when the Way matched Heaven and Earth—this was the pinnacle of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 後世禮法不修，刑政苛紊，代變新聲，導欲增悲，故有輕生敗倫不可禁者矣。

translations.literal: Later ages did not cultivate ritual law; punishments and government were harsh and tangled; generations changed to new sounds, guiding desire and increasing grief—hence there are those who lightly abandon life and destroy human relations, impossible to prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages ritual law fell into neglect, punishments and governance grew harsh and chaotic, and each generation produced new sounds that stirred desire and deepened sorrow—giving rise to those who lightly abandoned life and violated human relations beyond all prohibition.

sentences.zh: 樂者，古以平心，今以助欲；

translations.literal: Music—in antiquity used to level the mind, today used to aid desire;
translations.idiomatic: Music—in antiquity served to calm the mind; today it serves to inflame desire;

sentences.zh: 古以宣化，今以長怨。

translations.literal: in antiquity used to disseminate transformation, today used to lengthen resentment.
translations.idiomatic: in antiquity it disseminated moral transformation; today it deepens resentment.

sentences.zh: 不復古禮，不變今樂，而欲至治者，遠哉！”

translations.literal: Not restoring ancient ritual, not changing present music, yet wishing to reach perfect governance—how far!
translations.idiomatic: Without restoring ancient ritual or reforming present music, yet hoping to achieve perfect governance—how remote that prospect!

sentences.zh: 程頤有曰：“律者，自然之數。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi had words: "Pitch standards are Nature's numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi remarked: "Pitch standards are numbers inherent in Nature.

sentences.zh: 先王之樂，必須律以考其聲。

translations.literal: The former kings' music must use pitch standards to examine its sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The music of the former kings must be tested against pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 尺度權衡之正，皆起於律。

translations.literal: The correctness of measures, feet, and balances all arise from pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: The correctness of measures, weights, and balances all derives from pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 律管定尺，以天地之氣為準，非黍之比也。

translations.literal: The pitch-standard tube fixes the foot, taking Heaven and Earth's qi as standard—not millet's comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-standard tube determines the foot measure, taking the qi of Heaven and Earth as the standard—not the proportions of millet grains.

sentences.zh: 律取黃鍾，黃鍾之聲亦不難定，有知音者，參上下聲考之，自得其正。”

translations.literal: Pitch standards take Huangzhong; Huangzhong's sound is also not hard to fix—one who understands sound, comparing upper and lower sounds to examine it, naturally obtains its correctness.
translations.idiomatic: The standard takes Huangzhong; Huangzhong's pitch is not difficult to determine—one who understands music, comparing higher and lower tones, will naturally arrive at the correct pitch.

sentences.zh: 張載有曰：“聲音之道與天地通，蠶吐絲而商弦絕，木氣盛則金氣衰，乃此理自相應。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai had words: "The way of sound connects with Heaven and Earth; the silkworm spits silk and the shang string breaks, wood qi flourishing then metal qi declines—this principle naturally corresponds to itself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai remarked: "The way of sound connects with Heaven and Earth. When silkworms spin silk, the shang string breaks; when wood qi flourishes, metal qi declines—such is the mutual correspondence of this principle.

sentences.zh: 今人求古樂太深，始以古樂為不可知，律呂有可求之理，惟德性深厚者能知之。”

translations.literal: Present people seeking ancient music too deeply begin to take ancient music as unknowable—yet lü and lü have a principle that can be sought; only those of deep virtue and nature can know it."
translations.idiomatic: People today pursue ancient music so obsessively that they conclude it is unknowable. Yet pitch standards have principles that can be discovered—only those of profound moral cultivation can grasp them."

sentences.zh: 此三臣之學，可謂窮本知變，達樂之要者矣。

translations.literal: These three ministers' learning can be called exhausting the root and knowing change, reaching music's essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The learning of these three masters may be said to have penetrated fundamentals, understood transformation, and grasped the essentials of music.

sentences.zh: 熹與元定蓋深講於其學者，而研覃真積，述為成書。

translations.literal: Xi and Yuanding broadly deeply expounded this learning, and through profound study and true accumulation, narrated it into a completed book.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Yuanding engaged deeply with this tradition, pursuing sustained study until they composed a definitive work.

sentences.zh: 元定先究律呂本原，分其篇目，又從而證辨之。

translations.literal: Yuanding first investigated lü and lü's origin, divided its chapters, and further verified and distinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding first investigated the origins of pitch standards, organized them into chapters, and then provided detailed verification and analysis.

sentences.zh: 其黃鍾篇曰：

translations.literal: His Huangzhong chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: His chapter on Huangzhong states:

sentences.zh: 天地之數始於一，終於十：其一、三、五、七、九為陽，九者，陽之成也；

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth's numbers begin at one, end at ten: one, three, five, seven, nine are yang—nine is yang's completion;
translations.idiomatic: The numbers of Heaven and Earth begin at one and end at ten: one, three, five, seven, and nine are yang—nine being the completion of yang;

sentences.zh: 其二、四、六、八、十為陰，十者，陰之成也。

translations.literal: two, four, six, eight, ten are yin—ten is yin's completion.
translations.idiomatic: two, four, six, eight, and ten are yin—ten being the completion of yin.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾者，陽聲之始，陽氣之動也，故其數九。

translations.literal: Huangzhong is yang sound's beginning, yang qi's movement—hence its number is nine.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong is the beginning of yang sound, the movement of yang qi—hence its number is nine.

sentences.zh: 分寸之數，具於聲氣之先，不可得而見。

translations.literal: The numbers of inches and parts exist before sound and qi, impossible to obtain and see.
translations.idiomatic: The numerical proportions of length exist prior to sound and qi, and cannot be perceived directly.

sentences.zh: 及斷竹為管，吹之而聲和，候之而氣應，而後數始形焉。

translations.literal: When cutting bamboo for a tube, blowing it and the sound harmonizes, observing it and the qi responds—then afterward the numbers first take form.
translations.idiomatic: Only when bamboo is cut into a tube, blown until the sound harmonizes, and observed until the qi responds do the numbers first take visible form.

sentences.zh: 均其長，得九寸；

translations.literal: Balancing its length, one obtains nine inches;
translations.idiomatic: Balancing its length yields nine inches;

sentences.zh: 審其圍，得九分；

translations.literal: examining its circumference, nine tenths;
translations.idiomatic: measuring its circumference yields nine tenths of an inch;

sentences.zh: 積其實，得八百一十分。

translations.literal: accumulating its volume, eight hundred and ten tenths.
translations.idiomatic: and calculating its volume yields eight hundred and ten cubic tenths of an inch.

sentences.zh: 長九寸，圍九分，積八百一十分，是為律本，度量權衡於是而受法，十一律由是損益焉。

translations.literal: Length nine inches, circumference nine tenths, volume eight hundred and ten tenths—this is the pitch standard's root; measures, feet, and balances thereby receive their law; the eleven pitch standards thereby are increased or decreased.
translations.idiomatic: Nine inches in length, nine tenths in circumference, eight hundred and ten tenths in volume—this is the fundamental pitch standard. Measures, weights, and balances derive their standards from it, and the eleven pitch standards are adjusted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：古者考聲候氣，皆以聲之清濁、氣之先後求黃鍾也。

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: In antiquity examining sound and observing qi both used sound's clarity and murkiness, qi's precedence and succession, to seek Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: In antiquity, examining sound and observing qi both relied on the clarity or murkiness of sound and the precedence or succession of qi to determine Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 夫律長則聲濁而氣先至，律短則聲清而氣後至，極長極短則不成聲而氣不應。

translations.literal: When the pitch standard is long, the sound is murky and qi arrives first; when short, the sound is clear and qi arrives later; at extreme length or extreme shortness, sound is not formed and qi does not respond.
