translations.idiomatic: When the pitch tube is too long, the sound is murky and qi arrives early; when too short, the sound is clear and qi arrives late. At extremes of length, no proper sound forms and qi fails to respond.

sentences.zh: 今欲求聲氣之中，而莫適為準，莫若且多截竹以擬黃鍾之管，或極其短，或極其長，長短之內，每差一分而為一管，皆即以其長權為九寸，而度圍徑如黃鍾之法焉。

translations.literal: Now wishing to seek the middle of sound and qi yet having nothing suitable as standard, nothing is better than first cutting much bamboo to approximate Huangzhong's tube—either at its extreme short or extreme long; within long and short, each differing one fen making one tube—all taking its length as weight for nine inches, and measuring circumference and diameter by Huangzhong's method.
translations.idiomatic: To find the mean between sound and qi when no suitable standard exists, one should cut many bamboo tubes approximating the Huangzhong standard—some extremely short, some extremely long. Within this range, make one tube for each fen of difference, proportioning each length to nine inches and measuring circumference and diameter by the Huangzhong method.

sentences.zh: 更迭以吹，則中聲可得；

translations.literal: Alternately blowing them, then the middle sound can be obtained;
translations.idiomatic: Blowing them in succession, the correct middle pitch can be found;

sentences.zh: 淺深以列，則中氣可驗。

translations.literal: Arranging shallow and deep in sequence, then the middle qi can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: By arranging them according to depth of tone, the correct middle qi can be verified.

sentences.zh: 苟聲和氣應，則黃鍾之為黃鍾者信矣。

translations.literal: If sound harmonizes and qi responds, then that Huangzhong is truly Huangzhong is confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: If sound and qi accord, one can be confident that the tube is truly Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾信，則十一律與度量權衡者得矣。

translations.literal: Huangzhong confirmed, then the eleven pitch standards together with measures, feet, and balances are obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huangzhong is established, the eleven pitch standards and the systems of measure, weight, and balance can all be derived.

sentences.zh: 後世不知出此，而惟尺之求。

translations.literal: Later ages not knowing this emerged from it, but only sought by the foot-rule.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations, ignorant of this method, sought pitch standards solely through physical measurements.

sentences.zh: 晉氏而下，多求之金石；

translations.literal: From the Jin house downward, many sought it in metal and stone;
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin dynasty onward, scholars relied chiefly on metal and stone bells;

sentences.zh: 梁、隋以來，又參之黍；

translations.literal: from Liang and Sui onward, again mixed in millet;
translations.idiomatic: from the Liang and Sui dynasties onward, they also incorporated millet grains;

sentences.zh: 至王樸專恃累黍，金石亦不復考。

translations.literal: Reaching Wang Pu, he solely relied on stacked millet; metal and stone were also no longer examined.
translations.idiomatic: by the time of Wang Pu, scholars relied exclusively on stacked millet measures and ceased even to test metal and stone standards.

sentences.zh: 夫金石真偽固難盡信，而黍長短小大不同，尤不可恃。

translations.literal: Now metal and stone, true or false, are inherently hard to fully trust, while millet's length, shortness, size, and smallness differ—especially cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone artifacts are difficult to authenticate, and millet grains vary greatly in size; neither can be trusted.

sentences.zh: 古人謂‘子穀黍，中者實其籥’，是先得黃鍾而後度之以黍，以見周徑之度，以生度量權衡之數而已，非律生於黍也。

translations.literal: The ancients said 'millet of the son-grain, the middle one fills its tube'—this is first obtaining Huangzhong and afterward measuring it with millet, to see the circumference-and-diameter measure, to generate the numbers of measures, feet, and balances only; it is not that pitch standards are born from millet.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Use millet grains; the medium-sized grain fills the pitch tube.' They first established Huangzhong and only then used millet to measure it, thereby deriving circumference and diameter and producing the numbers for measures, weights, and balances—not deriving pitch standards from millet itself.

sentences.zh: 百世之下，欲求百世之前之律者，亦求之聲氣之元而毋必之於黍，斯得之矣。”）〉

translations.literal: A hundred generations below, wishing to seek a hundred generations before's pitch standards, also seek them in sound-and-qi's origin and need not insist on millet—thus obtaining them.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred generations later, anyone seeking to recover the pitch standards of antiquity should likewise seek the origin of sound and qi rather than insisting on millet; in that way the true standards may be found.

sentences.zh: 《黃鍾生十一律篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Huangzhong Generates the Eleven Pitch Standards' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Huangzhong Generates the Eleven Pitch Standards" states:

sentences.zh: 子、寅、辰、午、申、戌六陽辰皆下生，醜、卯、巳、未、酉、亥六陰辰皆上生。

translations.literal: Zi, yin, chen, wu, shen, and xu—the six yang earthly branches—all generate downward; chou, mao, si, wei, you, and hai—the six yin earthly branches—all generate upward.
translations.idiomatic: The six yang branches—zi, yin, chen, wu, shen, and xu—all generate pitch standards by downward progression; the six yin branches—chou, mao, si, wei, you, and hai—all generate by upward progression.

sentences.zh: 陽數以倍者，三分本律而損其一也；

translations.literal: Yang numbers use doubling: three-part the root pitch standard and diminish one part;
translations.idiomatic: For yang numbers, the method is doubling: take one-third of the fundamental pitch and subtract one part;

sentences.zh: 陰數以四者，三分本律而增其一也。

translations.literal: Yin numbers use fourfold: three-part the root pitch standard and augment one part.
translations.idiomatic: for yin numbers, the method is fourfold progression: take one-third of the fundamental pitch and add one part.

sentences.zh: 六陽辰當位，自得六陰位以居其衝。

translations.literal: The six yang earthly branches occupy their positions, each naturally obtaining a yin position to sit opposite.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the six yang branches occupies its proper position, paired with a yin branch in direct opposition.

sentences.zh: 其林鍾、南呂、應鍾三呂在陰，無所增損；

translations.literal: Among them Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong—the three lü in yin—have no augmenting or diminishing;
translations.idiomatic: Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong—the three yin pitch standards—undergo no augmentation or diminution;

sentences.zh: 其大呂、夾鍾、仲呂三呂在陽，則用倍數，方與十二月之氣相應，蓋陰陽自然之理也。

translations.literal: Dàlǚ, Jiazhong, and Zhonglü—the three lü in yang—then use doubling, only then corresponding to the twelve months' qi—covering yin-yang's natural principle.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Dàlǚ, Jiazhong, and Zhonglü—the three yang pitch standards—employ doubling, thereby corresponding to the qi of the twelve months. This reflects the natural principle of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“按《呂氏》、《淮南子》，上下相生，與司馬氏《律書》、《漢前志》不同，雖大呂、夾鍾、仲呂用倍數則一，然《呂氏》、《淮南》不過以數之多寡為生之上下，律呂陰陽錯亂而無倫，非其本法也。”）〉

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: "Examining the Lüshi [Chunqiu], the Huainanzi, upward-downward mutual generation differs from Sima Qian's "Treatise on Pitch Standards" and the Former Han Annals; although Dàlǚ, Jiazhong, and Zhonglü using doubling is the same, yet the Lüshi and Huainan only take numbers' more or less as generation's upward-downward—the pitch standards' yin-yang are disordered without principle, not their original method."
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: "The Lüshi Chunqiu and Huainanzi describe upward and downward generation differently from Sima Qian's Treatise on Pitch Standards and the Former Han Annals. Although they agree that Dàlǚ, Jiazhong, and Zhonglü use doubling, the Lüshi and Huainan merely treat numerical abundance or scarcity as the basis for upward or downward generation, disordering the yin-yang arrangement of the pitch standards. This is not the correct original method."

sentences.zh: 《十二律篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Twelve Pitch Standards' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "The Twelve Pitch Standards" states:

sentences.zh: 按十二律之實，約以寸法，則黃鍾、林鍾、太簇得全寸；

translations.literal: Examining the twelve pitch standards' volumes, approximating by the inch method, then Huangzhong, Linzhong, and Taicu obtain whole inches;
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the volumes of the twelve pitch standards: by the inch method, Huangzhong, Linzhong, and Taicu yield whole inches;

sentences.zh: 約以分法，則南呂、姑洗得全分；

translations.literal: approximating by the fen method, then Nanlü and Guxian obtain whole fen;
translations.idiomatic: by the fen method, Nanlü and Guxian yield whole fen;

sentences.zh: 約以厘法，則應鍾、蕤賓得全厘；

translations.literal: approximating by the li method, then Yingzhong and Ruibin obtain whole li;
translations.idiomatic: by the li method, Yingzhong and Ruibin yield whole li;

sentences.zh: 約以毫法，則大呂、夷則得全毫；

translations.literal: approximating by the hao method, then Dalü and Yize obtain whole hao;
translations.idiomatic: by the hao method, Dalü and Yize yield whole hao;

sentences.zh: 約以絲法，則夾鍾、無射得全絲。

translations.literal: approximating by the si method, then Jiazhong and Wushe obtain whole si.
translations.idiomatic: by the si method, Jiazhong and Wushe yield whole si.

sentences.zh: 約至仲呂之實十三萬一千七十二，以三分之，不盡二算，其數不行，此律之所以止於十二也。

translations.literal: Approximating to Zhonglü's volume one hundred thirty-one thousand seventy-two, dividing by three, not exhausting two counts—the number cannot proceed; this is why pitch standards stop at twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü's volume approximates to 131,072; divided by three, two counts remain undivided and the progression cannot continue. This is why the pitch standards end at twelve.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“黃鍾為十二律之首，他律無大於黃鍾，故其正聲不為他律役。

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: "Huangzhong is the head of the twelve pitch standards; no other standard is greater than Huangzhong, therefore its proper sound is not enslaved by other standards."
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: "Huangzhong stands first among the twelve pitch standards; no other standard surpasses it, and therefore its proper tone is not subordinate to any other standard."

sentences.zh: 至於大呂之變宮、夾鍾之羽、仲呂之徵、蕤賓之變征、夷則之角、無射之商，自用變律半聲，非復黃鍾矣。

translations.literal: As for Dalü's altered gong, Jiazhong's yu, Zhonglü's zhi, Ruibin's altered zhi, Yize's jue, and Wushe's shang—they themselves use altered pitch standards' half-sounds, no longer Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dalü's altered gong, Jiazhong's yu, Zhonglü's zhi, Ruibin's altered zhi, Yize's jue, and Wushe's shang all employ altered pitch standards and half-tones; they are no longer Huangzhong tones.

sentences.zh: 此其所以最尊而為君之象，然亦非人所能為，乃數之自然，他律雖欲役之而不可得也。

translations.literal: This is why it is most honored and bears the image of lord—yet it is also not what humans can make; it is number's naturalness; other standards though wishing to enslave it cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Huangzhong is supreme and symbolizes the sovereign—yet it is not a human contrivance but a necessity of number itself; other pitch standards cannot subordinate it even if they try.

sentences.zh: 此一節最為律呂旋宮用聲之綱領也。”）〉

translations.literal: This one section is most the guiding principle for pitch standards' circular palace and use of sounds.
translations.idiomatic: This passage is the essential principle governing the circular arrangement of pitch standards and the deployment of tones.

sentences.zh: 《變律篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Altered Pitch Standards' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Altered Pitch Standards" states:

sentences.zh: 十二律各自為宮，以生五聲二變。

translations.literal: The twelve pitch standards each serve as palace in turn, thereby generating the five sounds and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve pitch standards serves in turn as the tonal center, generating the five primary tones and the two altered tones.

sentences.zh: 其黃鍾、林鍾、太簇、南呂、姑洗、應鍾六律，則能具足。

translations.literal: Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, and Yingzhong—the six standards—then can be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, and Yingzhong—the six standards—can produce the full set of tones.

sentences.zh: 至蕤賓、大呂、夷則、夾鍾、無射、仲呂六律，則取黃鍾、林鍾、太簇、南呂、姑洗、應鍾六律之聲，少下，不和，故有變律。

translations.literal: Reaching Ruibin, Dalü, Yize, Jiazhong, Wushe, and Zhonglü—the six standards—then take Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, and Yingzhong's six standards' sounds, slightly lower, not harmonizing—therefore there are altered pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: For Ruibin, Dalü, Yize, Jiazhong, Wushe, and Zhonglü, borrowing tones from the first six standards produces pitches slightly too low and out of harmony; hence altered pitch standards are required.

sentences.zh: 律之當變者有六：黃鍾、林鍾、太簇、南呂、姑洗、應鍾。

translations.literal: Standards that ought to be altered are six: Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, Yingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Six pitch standards require alteration: Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, and Yingzhong.

sentences.zh: 變律者，其聲近正律而少高於正律，然後洪纖、高下不相奪倫。

translations.literal: Altered pitch standards: their sounds are near proper standards yet slightly higher than proper standards—only then do great and fine, high and low, not seize each other's order.
translations.idiomatic: Altered pitch standards produce tones close to the proper standards but slightly higher, so that loud and soft, high and low, do not violate their proper hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 變律非正律，故不為宮。

translations.literal: Altered pitch standards are not proper standards, therefore they do not serve as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Altered pitch standards are not proper standards and therefore cannot serve as the tonal center.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“十二律循環相生，而世俗不知三分損益之數，往而不返。

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: "The twelve pitch standards cyclically generate one another, yet the vulgar world does not know the three-part diminish-and-augment numbers—going but not returning."
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: "The twelve pitch standards generate one another in a cycle, but common scholars do not understand the mathematics of three-part diminish-and-augment progression, which advances without returning."

sentences.zh: 仲呂再生黃鍾，止得八寸七分有奇，不成黃鍾正聲。

translations.literal: Zhonglü again generating Huangzhong obtains only eight inches seven fen and a fraction—does not form Huangzhong's proper sound.
translations.idiomatic: Regenerating Huangzhong from Zhonglü yields only eight and seven-tenths odd inches, not the proper Huangzhong tone.

sentences.zh: 京房覺其如此，故仲呂再生，別名執始，轉生四十八律。

translations.literal: Jing Fang perceived it thus, therefore Zhonglü's regeneration was separately named Zhishi, turning to generate forty-eight pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang recognized this problem and, when regenerating from Zhonglü, named the new standard Zhishi and proceeded to generate forty-eight pitch standards in succession.

sentences.zh: 不知變律之數止於六者，出於自然，不可復加。

translations.literal: Not knowing that altered pitch standards' number stopping at six emerges from nature and cannot again be added.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to see that the six altered pitch standards arise from natural necessity and cannot be increased.

sentences.zh: 雖強加之，亦無所用也。

translations.literal: Though forcibly adding them, they are also of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Even if more were forcibly added, they would serve no purpose.

sentences.zh: 房之所傳出於焦氏，焦氏卦氣之學，亦去四而為六十，故其推律必求合此數。

translations.literal: What Fang transmitted came from the Jiao clan; the Jiao clan's hexagram-qi learning also removed four to make sixty—therefore his deriving pitch standards must seek to match this number.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's doctrine derived from the Jiao clan, whose hexagram-qi theory also reduces the cycle to sixty by removing four; hence his pitch calculations were compelled to conform to that number.

sentences.zh: 不知數之自然，在律不可增，於卦不可減也。

translations.literal: Not knowing number's naturalness: in pitch standards cannot be increased, in hexagrams cannot be diminished.
translations.idiomatic: He did not understand that these numbers follow natural law: pitch standards cannot be augmented, nor can hexagram cycles be arbitrarily reduced.

sentences.zh: 何承天、劉焯譏房之病，乃欲增林鍾已下十一律之分，使至仲呂反生黃鍾，還得十七萬七千一百四十七之數，則是惟黃鍾一律成律，他十一律皆不應三分損益之數，其失又甚於房。）〉

translations.literal: He Chengtian and Liu Chuo criticized Fang's flaw, yet wished to increase Linzhong and below's eleven standards' divisions, making it so that reaching Zhonglü in turn generating Huangzhong again obtained the number one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven—then only Huangzhong one standard formed a standard; the other eleven standards all did not respond to three-part diminish-and-augment numbers; their error was again worse than Fang's.) [End of editorial commentary.]
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian and Liu Chuo criticized Fang's error yet proposed increasing the fractional divisions of the eleven standards below Linzhong so that regenerating Huangzhong from Zhonglü would restore the number 177,147—leaving only Huangzhong as a true standard while the other eleven failed to conform to three-part diminish-and-augment mathematics. Their error was even graver than Fang's.) [End of editorial commentary.]

sentences.zh: 《律生五聲篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Pitch Standards Generate the Five Sounds' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Pitch Standards Generate the Five Sounds" states:

sentences.zh: 宮聲八十一，商聲七十二，角聲六十四，徵聲五十四，羽聲四十八。

translations.literal: Gong sound eighty-one, shang sound seventy-two, jue sound sixty-four, zhi sound fifty-four, yu sound forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The gong tone is 81, the shang tone 72, the jue tone 64, the zhi tone 54, and the yu tone 48.

sentences.zh: 按黃鍾之數九九八十一，是為五聲之原，三分損一以下生徵，徵三分益一以上生商，商三分損一以下生羽，羽三分益一以上生角。

translations.literal: Examining Huangzhong's number nine-nine eighty-one—this is the five sounds' origin: three-part diminish one part to generate downward zhi; zhi three-part augment one part to generate upward shang; shang three-part diminish one part to generate downward yu; yu three-part augment one part to generate upward jue.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong's number is 9 × 9 = 81, the origin of the five tones. Diminishing by one-third generates the zhi tone downward; augmenting zhi by one-third generates shang upward; diminishing shang by one-third generates yu downward; augmenting yu by one-third generates jue upward.

sentences.zh: 至角聲之數六十四，以三分之，不盡一算，數不可行，此聲之數所以止於五也。

translations.literal: Reaching jue sound's number sixty-four, dividing by three, not exhausting one count—the number cannot proceed; this is why sounds' number stops at five.
translations.idiomatic: The jue tone's number is 64; divided by three, one count remains undivided and the progression cannot continue. This is why there are only five primary tones.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“《通典》曰：‘黃鍾為均，用五聲之法以下十一辰，辰各有五聲，其為宮商之法亦如之。

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: "The Tongdian says: 'Huangzhong as jun, applying the five sounds' method to the eleven earthly branches below—each branch has five sounds; the method for gong and shang is likewise.'"
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: "The Tongdian says: 'With Huangzhong as the standard pitch, apply the method of the five tones to the eleven branches below; each branch has five tones, and the methods for gong and shang follow the same principle.'"

sentences.zh: 辰各有五聲，合為六十聲，是十二律之正聲也。

translations.literal: Each branch has five sounds, combined as sixty sounds—this is the twelve pitch standards' proper sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Each branch has five tones, totaling sixty tones—the proper sounds of the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: ’夫黃鍾一均之數，而十一律於此取法焉。

translations.literal: ' Now Huangzhong is one jun's number, and the eleven pitch standards take their law from this.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong provides the single standard number from which the eleven other pitch standards derive their proportions.

sentences.zh: 以十二律之宮長短不同，而其臣、民、事、物、尊卑，莫不有序而不相亂，良以是耳。

translations.literal: Because the twelve pitch standards' palaces' lengths differ, yet their ministers, people, affairs, things, honor and baseness—all without disorder and not mutually confused—truly because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tonal centers of the twelve pitch standards differ in length, the hierarchical relationships among minister, commoner, affair, and object—high and low—remain ordered and distinct. This is precisely why.

sentences.zh: 沈括不知此理，乃以為五十四在黃鍾為徵、在夾鍾為角、在仲呂為商者，其亦誤矣。

translations.literal: Shen Kuo did not know this principle, yet thought that fifty-four in Huangzhong is zhi, in Jiazhong is jue, in Zhonglü is shang—he too erred.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kuo failed to understand this principle and mistakenly held that the number 54 represents zhi in Huangzhong, jue in Jiazhong, and shang in Zhonglü.

sentences.zh: 俗樂之有清聲，略知此意。

translations.literal: Vulgar music's having clear sounds slightly knows this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Popular music's use of clear tones reflects a partial grasp of this principle.

sentences.zh: 但不知仲呂反生黃鍾，黃鍾又自林鍾再生太簇，皆為變律，已非黃鍾、太簇之清聲耳。

translations.literal: But not knowing Zhonglü in turn generating Huangzhong, Huangzhong again from Linzhong regenerating Taicu—all are altered pitch standards, already not Huangzhong and Taicu's clear sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they do not realize that regenerating Huangzhong from Zhonglü or Taicu from Linzhong via Huangzhong produces altered pitch standards, not the clear tones of Huangzhong and Taicu proper.

sentences.zh: 胡瑗於四清聲皆小其圍徑，則黃鍾、太簇二聲雖合，而大呂、夾鍾二聲又非本律之半。

translations.literal: Hu Yuan, regarding the four clear sounds all reducing their circumference and diameter—then Huangzhong and Taicu's two sounds though accord, yet Dalü and Jiazhong's two sounds again are not the root standards' halves.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan reduced the circumference of all four clear-tone pipes; although Huangzhong and Taicu then matched, Dalü and Jiazhong no longer represented true half-lengths of their fundamental standards.

sentences.zh: 且自夷則至應鍾四律，皆以次而小其徑圍以就之，遂使十二律、五聲皆有不得其正者。

translations.literal: Moreover from Yize to Yingzhong four standards, all in sequence reducing circumference and diameter to accommodate—thereby making the twelve pitch standards and five sounds all have some not obtaining their proper.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, from Yize through Yingzhong he progressively reduced the circumference of four standards to make them fit, so that none of the twelve pitch standards or five tones remained properly tuned.

sentences.zh: 李照、範鎮止用十二律，則又未知此理。

translations.literal: Li Zhao and Fan Zhen only using the twelve pitch standards—then again not knowing this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao and Fan Zhen, who used only the twelve pitch standards, were equally ignorant of this principle.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂之和者，在於三分損益；

translations.literal: For music's harmony lies in three-part diminish-and-augment;
translations.idiomatic: Harmony in music depends on three-part diminish-and-augment;

sentences.zh: 樂之辨者，在於上下相生。

translations.literal: music's distinction lies in upward-downward mutual generation.
translations.idiomatic: while distinction in music depends on upward and downward generation among the standards.

sentences.zh: 若李照、範鎮之法，其合於三分損益者則和矣，自夷則已降，其臣、民、事、物，豈能尊卑有辨而不相淩犯乎？

translations.literal: If Li Zhao and Fan Zhen's methods—what accords with three-part diminish-and-augment is harmonious; from Yize downward, their ministers, people, affairs, things—how can honor and baseness have distinction and not mutually encroach?
translations.idiomatic: Under the methods of Li Zhao and Fan Zhen, tones conforming to three-part diminish-and-augment may be harmonious, but from Yize downward, how could the hierarchical relationships of minister, commoner, affair, and object retain proper distinction without mutual violation?

sentences.zh: 晉荀勖之笛，梁武帝之通，皆不知而作者也。”）〉

translations.literal: Jin Xun Xu's flute, Liang Wudi's tong—all composed without knowing.
translations.idiomatic: The flutes of Jin's Xun Xu and the pitch pipes of Liang's Emperor Wu were likewise devised in ignorance of this principle.

sentences.zh: 《變聲篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Altered Sounds' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Altered Sounds" states:

sentences.zh: 變宮聲四十二，變徵聲五十六。

translations.literal: Altered gong sound forty-two, altered zhi sound fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The altered gong tone is 42; the altered zhi tone is 56.

sentences.zh: 五聲宮與商、商與角、徵與羽相去各一律，至角與徵、羽與宮相去乃二律。

translations.literal: Among the five sounds, gong and shang, shang and jue, zhi and yu are separated each by one pitch standard; reaching jue and zhi, yu and gong—the separation is then two standards.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five tones, gong and shang, shang and jue, and zhi and yu are each one pitch standard apart; but jue and zhi, and yu and gong, are two standards apart.

sentences.zh: 相去一律則音節和，相去二律則音節遠。

translations.literal: Separated by one standard then the musical interval is harmonious; separated by two standards then the musical interval is distant.
translations.idiomatic: A separation of one standard produces harmonious intervals; a separation of two standards produces distant intervals.

sentences.zh: 故角、徽之間，近徵收一聲，比徵少下，故謂之變徵；

translations.literal: Therefore between jue and zhi, near zhi gather one sound, compared to zhi slightly lower—therefore called altered zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore between jue and zhi, a tone is drawn toward zhi but placed slightly below it; this is called the altered zhi;

sentences.zh: 羽、宮之間，近宮收一聲，少高於宮，故謂之變宮。

translations.literal: Between yu and gong, near gong gather one sound, slightly higher than gong—therefore called altered gong.
translations.idiomatic: between yu and gong, a tone is drawn toward gong but placed slightly above it; this is called the altered gong.

sentences.zh: 角聲之實六十有四，以三分之，不盡一算，既不可行，當有以通之。

translations.literal: Jue sound's volume sixty-four, dividing by three, not exhausting one count—already cannot proceed; there ought to be means to penetrate it.
translations.idiomatic: The jue tone's volume is 64; divided by three, one count remains undivided and the progression cannot continue. A method must be found to resolve this.

sentences.zh: 聲之變者二，故置一而兩，三之得九，以九因角聲之實六十有四，得五百七十六。

translations.literal: Sounds' alterations are two; therefore set one to make two, three it obtaining nine, use nine to multiply jue sound's volume sixty-four, obtaining five hundred seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: There are two altered tones; therefore one is doubled to make two, and tripling yields nine. Multiplying the jue volume of 64 by 9 gives 576.

sentences.zh: 三分損益，再生變徵、變宮二聲，以九歸之，以從五聲之數，存其餘數，以為強弱。

translations.literal: Three-part diminish-and-augment, again generating altered zhi and altered gong's two sounds, use nine to return them, to follow the five sounds' numbers, preserving the remainder numbers as strong and weak.
translations.idiomatic: By three-part diminish-and-augment, the two altered tones—altered zhi and altered gong—are generated; dividing by 9 aligns them with the five-tone system, and the remainders indicate relative strength.

sentences.zh: 至變徵之數五百一十二，以三分之，又不盡二算，其數又不行，此變聲所以止於二也。

translations.literal: Reaching altered zhi's number five hundred twelve, dividing by three, again not exhausting two counts—the number again cannot proceed; this is why altered sounds stop at two.
translations.idiomatic: The altered zhi tone's number is 512; divided by three, two counts remain undivided and the progression again cannot continue. This is why there are only two altered tones.

sentences.zh: 變宮、變徵，宮不成宮，徵不成徵，《淮南子》謂之“和謬”，所以濟五聲之不及也。

translations.literal: Altered gong and altered zhi—gong does not form gong, zhi does not form zhi; the Huainanzi calls them "harmonic dissonance"—therefore to aid the five sounds' insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Altered gong and altered zhi are neither true gong nor true zhi; the Huainanzi calls them "harmonic dissonance," bridging the gaps that the five primary tones cannot fill.

sentences.zh: 變聲非正聲，故不為調。

translations.literal: Altered sounds are not proper sounds, therefore they do not form modes.
translations.idiomatic: Altered tones are not proper tones and therefore cannot serve as modal centers.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“宮、羽之間有變宮，角、徵之間有變徵，此亦出於自然，《左氏》所謂‘七音’，《漢前志》所謂“七始”是也。

translations.literal: (His "Verification and Distinction" says: "Between gong and yu there is altered gong; between jue and zhi there is altered zhi—this too emerges from nature; what the Zuoshi [Chunqiu] calls 'seven sounds,' what the Former Han Annals calls 'seven origins'—is this."
translations.idiomatic: (His "Verification and Distinction" states: "Between gong and yu stands altered gong; between jue and zhi stands altered zhi. These too arise from natural law—the 'seven sounds' of the Zuo Commentary and the 'seven origins' of the Former Han Annals refer to this."

sentences.zh: 然五聲者，正聲，故以起調、畢曲，為諸聲之綱。

translations.literal: Yet the five sounds are proper sounds, therefore used to begin modes and conclude pieces—as all sounds' guiding principle.
translations.idiomatic: The five primary tones are proper tones; they open and close musical modes and serve as the governing framework for all sounds.

sentences.zh: 至二變聲，則不比於正音，但可濟其所不及而已。

translations.literal: Reaching the two altered sounds, they are not compared to proper sounds, but can only aid what they do not reach.
translations.idiomatic: The two altered tones are not ranked with proper tones; they merely supplement what the primary tones cannot achieve.

sentences.zh: 然有五聲而無二變，亦不可以成樂也。”）〉

translations.literal: Yet having the five sounds without the two alterations also cannot complete music.
translations.idiomatic: Yet music cannot be complete with only the five primary tones and without the two altered tones.

sentences.zh: 《八十四聲篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Eighty-Four Sounds' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Eighty-Four Sounds" states:

sentences.zh: 黃鍾不為他律役，所用七聲皆正律，無空、積、忽、微。

translations.literal: Huangzhong is not enslaved by other standards; the seven sounds used are all proper standards—without void, accumulation, neglect, or minute.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong is not subordinate to other standards; all seven tones it employs are proper standards, free of void, accumulated, neglected, or minute discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 自林鍾而下，則有半聲：大呂、太簇一半聲，夾鍾、姑洗二半聲，蕤賓、林鍾四半聲，夷則、南呂五半聲，無射、應鍾為六半聲。

translations.literal: From Linzhong downward, then there are half-sounds: Dalü and Taicu one half-sound, Jiazhong and Guxian two half-sounds, Ruibin and Linzhong four half-sounds, Yize and Nanlü five half-sounds, Wushe and Yingzhong as six half-sounds.
translations.idiomatic: From Linzhong downward, half-tones appear: Dalü and Taicu require one half-tone; Jiazhong and Guxian require two; Ruibin and Linzhong require four; Yize and Nanlü require five; Wushe and Yingzhong require six.

sentences.zh: 中呂為十二律之窮，三半聲也。

translations.literal: Zhonglü is the twelve pitch standards' extremity—three half-sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü marks the limit of the twelve pitch standards, requiring three half-tones.

sentences.zh: 自蕤賓而下則有變律：蕤賓一變律，大呂二變律，夷則三變律，夾鍾四變律，無射五變律，中呂六變律也。

translations.literal: From Ruibin downward then there are altered pitch standards: Ruibin one altered standard, Dalü two altered standards, Yize three altered standards, Jiazhong four altered standards, Wushe five altered standards, Zhonglü six altered standards.
translations.idiomatic: From Ruibin downward come altered pitch standards: Ruibin requires one; Dalü requires two; Yize requires three; Jiazhong requires four; Wushe requires five; Zhonglü requires six.

sentences.zh: 皆有空、積、忽、微，不得其正，故黃鍾獨為聲氣之元。

translations.literal: All have void, accumulation, neglect, and minute—not obtaining their proper; therefore Huangzhong alone is sound-and-qi's origin.
translations.idiomatic: All suffer void, accumulated, neglected, and minute errors and fail to achieve proper pitch; therefore Huangzhong alone remains the origin of sound and qi.

sentences.zh: 雖十二律八十四聲皆黃鍾所生，然黃鍾一均，所謂純粹中之純粹者也。

translations.literal: Although the twelve pitch standards' eighty-four sounds are all Huangzhong-generated, yet Huangzhong's one jun is what is called pure within pure.
translations.idiomatic: Although all eighty-four sounds of the twelve pitch standards derive from Huangzhong, Huangzhong's single standard pitch is the purest among the pure.

sentences.zh: 八十四聲：正律六十三，變律二十一。

translations.literal: Eighty-four sounds: proper standards sixty-three, altered standards twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Of the eighty-four sounds, sixty-three belong to proper standards and twenty-one to altered standards.

sentences.zh: 六十三者，九七之數也；

translations.literal: Sixty-three is nine-times-seven's number;
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-three is the product of 9 and 7;

sentences.zh: 二十一者，三七之數也。

translations.literal: twenty-one is three-times-seven's number.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-one is the product of 3 and 7.

sentences.zh: 《六十調篇》曰：

translations.literal: The 'Sixty Modes' chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Sixty Modes" states:

sentences.zh: 十二律旋相為宮，各有七聲，合八十四聲。

translations.literal: The twelve pitch standards in rotation each serve as palace; each has seven sounds, combined as eighty-four sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pitch standards rotate as tonal centers; each produces seven tones, totaling eighty-four sounds.

sentences.zh: 宮聲十二，商聲十二，角聲十二，徵聲十二，羽聲十二，凡六十聲，為六十調，其變宮十二，在羽聲之後、宮聲之前；

translations.literal: Gong sounds twelve, shang sounds twelve, jue sounds twelve, zhi sounds twelve, yu sounds twelve—in all sixty sounds, forming sixty modes; their altered gong twelve, placed after yu sounds and before gong sounds;
translations.idiomatic: There are twelve gong tones, twelve shang, twelve jue, twelve zhi, and twelve yu—sixty tones in all, constituting the sixty modes. The twelve altered gong tones fall after the yu tones and before the gong tones;

sentences.zh: 變徵十二，在角聲之後、徵聲之前：宮徵皆不成，凡二十四聲，不可為調。

translations.literal: altered-zhi twelve, at jiao-tone's after, zhi-tone's before: gong-zhi all not complete, altogether twenty-four tones, cannot serve as modes.
translations.idiomatic: There are twelve altered-zhi tones, set after the jiao tone and before the zhi tone: neither gong nor zhi can be fully established; all twenty-four such tones cannot serve as modes.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾宮至夾鍾羽，並用黃鍾起調、黃鍾畢曲；

translations.literal: Yellow Bell gong to Compressed Bell yu, all use Yellow Bell to raise mode, Yellow Bell to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: From Yellow Bell gong through Compressed Bell yu, every mode takes Yellow Bell to open the tune and Yellow Bell to close it;

sentences.zh: 大呂宮至姑洗羽，並用大呂起調、大呂畢曲；

translations.literal: Great Clay gong to Maiden Wash yu, all use Great Clay to raise mode, Great Clay to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: From Great Clay gong through Maiden Wash yu, each relies on Great Clay both to begin the mode and to finish the melody;

sentences.zh: 太簇宮至仲呂，並用太簇起調、太簇畢曲；

translations.literal: Great Cluster gong to Mid Bell, all use Great Cluster to raise mode, Great Cluster to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: From Great Cluster gong through Mid Bell, the mode is raised with Great Cluster and concluded with Great Cluster;

sentences.zh: 夾鍾宮至蕤賓羽，並用夾鍾起調、夾鍾畢曲；

translations.literal: Compressed Bell gong to Luxuriant Guest yu, all use Compressed Bell to raise mode, Compressed Bell to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Compressed Bell gong through Luxuriant Guest yu likewise open and close upon Compressed Bell alone;

sentences.zh: 姑洗宮至林鍾羽，並用姑洗起調、姑洗畢曲；

translations.literal: Maiden Wash gong to Forest Bell yu, all use Maiden Wash to raise mode, Maiden Wash to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: For Maiden Wash gong down to Forest Bell yu, Maiden Wash alone sets the opening key and seals the cadence;

sentences.zh: 仲呂宮至夷則羽，並用仲呂起調、仲呂畢曲；

translations.literal: Mid Bell gong to Level Rule yu, all use Mid Bell to raise mode, Mid Bell to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Mid Bell gong through Level Rule yu are governed throughout by Mid Bell for both the opening and the final stroke;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓宮至南呂羽，並用蕤賓起調、蕤賓畢曲；

translations.literal: Luxuriant Guest gong to Southern Bell yu, all use Luxuriant Guest to raise mode, Luxuriant Guest to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Luxuriant Guest gong to Southern Bell yu share one rule: Luxuriant Guest raises the mode and Luxuriant Guest ends the piece;

sentences.zh: 林鍾宮至無射羽，並用林鍾起調、林鍾畢曲；

translations.literal: Forest Bell gong to Untempered yu, all use Forest Bell to raise mode, Forest Bell to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Between Forest Bell gong and Untempered yu, Forest Bell alone marks where the tune begins and where it ends;

sentences.zh: 夷則宮至應鍾羽，並用夷則起調、夷則畢曲；

translations.literal: Level Rule gong to Responding Bell yu, all use Level Rule to raise mode, Level Rule to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Level Rule gong through Responding Bell yu keep Level Rule as the tone that lifts the mode and the tone that closes the song;

sentences.zh: 南呂宮至黃鍾羽，並用南呂起調、南呂畢曲；

translations.literal: Southern Bell gong to Yellow Bell yu, all use Southern Bell to raise mode, Southern Bell to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Bell gong down to Yellow Bell yu still begin and end on Southern Bell for mode and cadence;

sentences.zh: 無射宮至大呂羽，並用無射起調、無射畢曲；

translations.literal: Untempered gong to Great Clay yu, all use Untempered to raise mode, Untempered to end piece;
translations.idiomatic: Untempered gong through Great Clay yu are bound to Untempered at the opening of the mode and at the piece's close;

sentences.zh: 應鍾宮至太簇羽，並用應鍾起調、應鍾畢曲，是為六十調。

translations.literal: Responding Bell gong to Great Cluster yu, all use Responding Bell to raise mode, Responding Bell to end piece; this is the sixty modes.
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell gong through Great Cluster yu likewise take Responding Bell to raise the mode and Responding Bell to finish the piece—thus are constituted the sixty modes.

sentences.zh: 六十調即十二律也，十二律即一黃鍾也。

translations.literal: sixty modes are the twelve pitches; the twelve pitches are one Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: The sixty modes are none other than the twelve pitches, and the twelve pitches are ultimately one Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾生十二律，十二律生五聲二變。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell generates twelve pitches; twelve pitches generate five tones and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell gives rise to the twelve pitches; the twelve pitches give rise to the five tones and the two alterations.

sentences.zh: 五聲各有紀綱，以成六十調，六十調皆黃鍾損益之變也。

translations.literal: five tones each have guiding principle, thereby completing sixty modes; sixty modes all are Yellow Bell diminish-increase's transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five tones has its own governing principle, and through them the sixty modes are completed; every mode is but a transformation wrought by diminishing and increasing Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 宮、商、角三十六調，老陽也；

translations.literal: gong, shang, jiao thirty-six modes, old yang;
translations.idiomatic: The thirty-six modes of gong, shang, and jiao belong to old yang;

sentences.zh: 其徵、羽二十四調，老陰也。

translations.literal: their zhi, yu twenty-four modes, old yin.
translations.idiomatic: the twenty-four modes of zhi and yu belong to old yin.

sentences.zh: 調成而陰陽備也。

translations.literal: modes complete and yin-yang provided.
translations.idiomatic: When the modes are complete, yin and yang are fully in place.

sentences.zh: 或曰：“日辰之數由天五、地六錯綜而生，律呂之數由黃鍾九寸損益而生，二者不同。

translations.literal: someone said: "day-and-branch numbers from Heaven Five, Earth Six interwoven arise; pitch-and-lü numbers from Yellow Bell nine inches diminish-increase arise; the two not same."
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "The numbers of days and branches arise from the interweaving of Heaven's five and Earth's six, while the numbers of pitches and lü arise from diminishing and increasing the nine inches of Yellow Bell—these two origins are not the same.

sentences.zh: 至數之成，則日有六甲、辰有五子為六十日；

translations.literal: when numbers complete, then days have six jia, branches have five zi as sixty days;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the reckoning is complete, the six jia of the days and the five zi of the branches together make sixty days;

sentences.zh: 律呂有六律、五聲為六十調，若合符節，何也？”

translations.literal: pitches-and-lü have six pitches, five tones as sixty modes—if matching tally and measure, how so?"
translations.idiomatic: and among pitches and lü the six pitches and five tones likewise yield sixty modes. If they accord so neatly, how is that?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“即所謂調成而陰陽備也。”

translations.literal: was said: "that is what is called modes complete and yin-yang provided."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "It is precisely what is meant by 'when the modes are complete, yin and yang are fully in place.'"

sentences.zh: 夫理必有對待，數之自然也。

translations.literal: Now principle must have counterpart; numbers' naturalness.
translations.idiomatic: In principle there must always be counterparts; such is the nature of number.

sentences.zh: 以天五、地六合陰與陽言之，則六甲、五子究於六十，其三十六為陽，二十四為陰。

translations.literal: taking Heaven Five, Earth Six joining yin and yang to speak, then six jia, five zi exhaust at sixty; of them thirty-six are yang, twenty-four are yin.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking in terms of Heaven's five and Earth's six joining yin and yang, the six jia and five zi together amount to sixty, of which thirty-six are yang and twenty-four are yin.

sentences.zh: 以黃鍾九寸紀陽不紀陰言之，則六律、五聲究於六十，亦三十六為陽，二十四為陰。

translations.literal: taking Yellow Bell nine inches recording yang not recording yin to speak, then six pitches, five tones exhaust at sixty, likewise thirty-six yang, twenty-four yin.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking in terms of the nine inches of Yellow Bell, which record yang but not yin, the six pitches and five tones likewise total sixty, again with thirty-six yang and twenty-four yin.

sentences.zh: 蓋一陽之中，又自有陰陽也。

translations.literal: for within one yang, again there is yin-yang of its own.
translations.idiomatic: For within a single yang there is yin and yang of its own once more.

sentences.zh: 非知天地之化育者，不能與於此。

translations.literal: not knowing Heaven-Earth's transforming-nurturing, one cannot participate in this.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who understand how Heaven and Earth transform and nurture all things can share in such understanding.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“《禮運》：‘五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮。

translations.literal: (His "Evidential Discrimination" says: "'Record of Rites: Evolution of Rites': 'five tones, six pitches, twelve tubes in turn each serve as gong."
translations.idiomatic: (In his Evidential Discrimination he writes: "The Record of Rites, 'Evolution of Rites,' states: 'The five tones, the six pitches, and the twelve tubes each in turn serve as gong.'"

sentences.zh: ’孔氏疏曰：‘黃鍾為第一宮，至中呂為第十二宮，各有五聲，凡六十聲。

translations.literal: ' Kong clan commentary says: 'Yellow Bell as first gong, to Mid Bell as twelfth gong; each has five tones, altogether sixty tones.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Kong Yingda's commentary explains: 'Yellow Bell is the first gong, and Mid Bell the twelfth; each has five tones, making sixty tones in all.'"

sentences.zh: ’聲者，所以起調、畢曲，為諸聲之綱領，正《禮運》所謂‘還相為宮’ 也。

translations.literal: ' A tone is that whereby one raises mode and ends piece; it is the guiding principle of all tones—precisely what 'Evolution of Rites' calls 'in turn each serve as gong.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The tone is what raises the mode and closes the piece; it is the head-thread of all tones—exactly what the Evolution of Rites means by 'each in turn serving as gong.'"

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大司樂》，祭祀不用商，惟宮、角、徵、羽四聲。

translations.literal: "Rites of Zhou: Grand Director of Music"—in sacrifice they do not use shang; only gong, jiao, zhi, yu four tones.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, "Grand Director of Music," records that in sacrifice shang is not used; only the four tones gong, jiao, zhi, and yu are employed.

sentences.zh: 古人變宮、變徵不為調，《左氏傳》曰：‘中聲以降，五降之後，不容彈矣。

translations.literal: ancients altered-gong, altered-zhi did not serve as modes; "Zuo Tradition" says: 'below the central tone, after five descents, no room to pluck.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did not treat altered gong and altered zhi as modes. The Zuo Tradition says: 'Below the central tone, after five descents there is no room left to play.'"

sentences.zh: ’以二變聲之不可為調也。

translations.literal: '—because the two alteration tones cannot serve as modes.
translations.idiomatic: '—because the two alteration tones cannot constitute modes.

sentences.zh: 後世以變宮、變徵參而為八十四調，其亦不考矣。”）〉

translations.literal: later ages took altered-gong, altered-zhi mixed to make eighty-four modes—they too did not examine.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations mixed altered gong and altered zhi into eighty-four modes; they too failed to investigate the matter properly."

sentences.zh: 《候氣篇》曰：

translations.literal: "Awaiting the Qi" chapter says:
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Awaiting the Qi" states:

sentences.zh: 以十二律分配節氣，按曆而俟之。

translations.literal: using twelve pitches to apportion solar terms, following calendar to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pitches are assigned to the solar terms, and one waits for them according to the calendar.

sentences.zh: 其氣之升，分、毫、絲、忽，隨節各異。

translations.literal: its qi's rising—fen, hao, si, hu—differs with each term.
translations.idiomatic: The rising of the qi differs by fen, hao, si, and hu with each solar term.

sentences.zh: 夫陽生於《復》，陰生於《後》，如環無端。

translations.literal: yang is born in "Return," yin is born in "After," like a ring without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yang is born in the hexagram Return; yin is born in the hexagram After; like a ring, they have no beginning or end.

sentences.zh: 今律呂之數，三分損益，終不復始，何也？

translations.literal: now pitch-and-lü numbers, one-third diminish-increase, in the end never return to start—how so?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the numbers of pitches and lü follow the method of diminishing and increasing by one-third, and in the end never return to the beginning—why is that?

sentences.zh: 曰：“陽之升始於子，午雖陰生，而陽之升於上者未已，至亥而後窮上反下；

translations.literal: was said: "yang's rising begins at zi; wu though yin is born, yet yang's rising above not yet ended, reaching hai only then exhausted above and turning below;
translations.idiomatic: The answer runs: "Yang's ascent begins at zi. At wuyin may be born, yet yang still continues rising above; only at hai does it exhaust the upper reach and turn back downward;

sentences.zh: 陰之升始於午，子雖陽生，而陰升於上亦未已，至巳而後窮上反下。

translations.literal: yin's rising begins at wu; zi though yang is born, yet yin's rising above also not ended, reaching si only then exhausted above and turning below.
translations.idiomatic: yin's ascent begins at wu. At zi yang may be born, yet yin likewise continues rising above; only at si does it exhaust the upper reach and turn back downward.

sentences.zh: 律於陰則不書，故終不復始也。

translations.literal: pitches regarding yin then are not written, therefore in the end never return to start.
translations.idiomatic: The pitches do not record yin, and therefore in the end they never return to the beginning."

sentences.zh: 是以升，陽之數，自子至巳差強，在律為尤強，在呂為差弱；

translations.literal: therefore in rising, yang's numbers from zi to si are somewhat strong—in pitch especially strong, in lü somewhat weak;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the rising phase, yang's numbers from zi to si are comparatively strong—strongest in the pitches (lü), somewhat weaker in the secondary tubes (lü in the yin sense);

sentences.zh: 自午至亥漸弱，在律為尤弱，在呂為差強。

translations.literal: from wu to hai gradually weak—in pitch especially weak, in lü somewhat strong.
translations.idiomatic: from wu to hai they gradually weaken—weakest in the pitches, somewhat stronger in the secondary tubes.

sentences.zh: 分數多寡，雖若不齊，然而絲分毫別，各有條理，此氣之所以飛灰，聲之所以中律也。”

translations.literal: fraction-numbers more or less, though seeming uneven, yet si-fen hao-bie each have pattern—this is why qi makes ash fly, why sound matches pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The fractional measures may seem uneven in quantity, yet divided to the finest si and hao each has its own pattern; this is why the qi makes the ash fly and why sound strikes the pitch true.

sentences.zh: 或曰：“《易》以道陰陽，而律不書陰，何也？”

translations.literal: someone said: "'Changes' takes yin-yang as its Way, yet pitches do not write yin—how so?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "The Changes expounds yin and yang, yet the pitches do not record yin—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“《易》盡天下之變，善惡無不備，律致中和之用，止於至善者也，以聲言之，大而至於雷霆，細而至於蠛蠓，無非聲也。

translations.literal: was said: "'Changes' exhausts all under Heaven's changes; good and evil none not provided. Pitches achieve central-harmony's function, stopping at utmost goodness. Speaking as sound, great reaching to thunderclap, fine reaching to gnat-midge—all none not sound."
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: "The Changes embraces every transformation under Heaven; good and evil alike are all included. The pitches aim at the function of central harmony and rest at utmost goodness. Considered as sound, they range from the thunderclap above to the gnat below—nothing is not sound."

sentences.zh: 《易》則無不備也，律則寫其所謂黃鍾一聲而已。

translations.literal: 'Changes' then has nothing not provided; pitches then inscribe only what is called Yellow Bell's one tone.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes leaves nothing out; the pitches inscribe only what is called the single tone of Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 雖有十二律六十調，然實一黃鍾也。

translations.literal: though there are twelve pitches sixty modes, yet in substance one Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are twelve pitches and sixty modes, in substance there is but one Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 是理也，在聲為中聲，在氣為中氣，在人則喜怒哀樂未發與發而中節，此聖人所以一天人、讚化育之道也。”

translations.literal: this principle: in sound it is central tone; in qi it is central qi; in person then joy-anger-sorrow-delight not yet released and released yet hitting measure—this is why the sage unifies Heaven-person, assists transforming-nurturing's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the principle: in sound it is the central tone; in qi the central qi; in the person, the joy, anger, sorrow, and delight neither yet expressed nor expressed but hitting the measure. This is how the sage unifies Heaven and humanity and assists the Way of transformation and nurture.

sentences.zh: 〈（其《證辨》曰：“律者，陽氣之動，陽聲之始，必聲和氣應，然後可以見天地之心。

translations.literal: (His "Evidential Discrimination" says: "Pitches are yang-qi's movement, yang-sound's beginning; sound and qi must respond, only then can one see Heaven-Earth's heart."
translations.idiomatic: (In his Evidential Discrimination he writes: "The pitches are the movement of yang qi and the beginning of yang sound; sound and qi must answer each other—only then can one discern the heart of Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 今不此之務，乃區區於黍之縱橫、古錢之大小，其亦難矣。

translations.literal: now not making this the task, yet fussing over millet's length-breadth, ancient coin's size—how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one does not pursue this but fusses instead over the length and breadth of millet grains or the size of ancient coins, how difficult the task becomes!"

sentences.zh: 然非精於曆數，則氣節亦未易正。”）〉

translations.literal: yet unless skilled in calendar-numbers, then qi-terms also not easy to rectify.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless one is skilled in calendrical reckoning, the qi and solar terms are not easily set right either."

sentences.zh: 至於審度量、謹權衡，會粹古今，辨析尤詳，皆所以參伍而定黃鍾為中聲之符驗也。

translations.literal: as for examining measures, strict weights-and-balances, gathering ancient-modern, discrimination especially detailed—all to cross-check and fix Yellow Bell as central tone's tally-proof.
translations.idiomatic: As for examining measures and weights with care, gathering ancient and modern learning, and discriminating with exceptional detail—all serve to cross-check and establish Yellow Bell as the proof-token of the central tone.

sentences.zh: 朱熹深好其書，謂國家行且平定，中原必將審音協律，以諧神人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi deeply favored his book, saying the state would soon be pacified; the Central Plain must examine tones harmonize pitches, thereby harmonizing spirits and humans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi greatly admired his book, declaring that as the state was about to be pacified, the Central Plain would surely examine tones and harmonize pitches to bring spirits and humanity into accord.

sentences.zh: 受詔典領之臣，宜得此書奏之，以備東都郊廟之樂。

translations.literal: imperial-mandate overseeing ministers ought obtain this book and memorialize it, to supply Eastern Capital suburban-altar music.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers charged by imperial mandate to oversee such matters ought to obtain this book and present it to the throne, that it might supply music for the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 熹定《鍾律》、《詩樂》、《樂製》、《樂舞》等篇，彙分於所修禮書中，皆聚古樂之根源，簡約可觀。

translations.literal: Xi fixed "Bell Pitches," "Ode Music," "Music Institutions," "Music Dance" and other chapters, collected and divided within his compiled ritual book—all gathering ancient music's roots, concise and worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi compiled the chapters "Bell Pitches," "Ode Music," "Music Institutions," and "Music Dance," among others, and distributed them through the ritual book he was editing; all gather the roots of ancient music in a concise form well worth reading.

sentences.zh: 而《鍾律》分前後篇，其前篇為條凡七：一曰十二律陰陽、辰位相生次第之圖，二曰十二律寸、分、厘、毫、絲、忽之數，三曰五聲五行之象、清濁高下之次，四曰五聲相生、損益、先後之次，五曰變宮、變徽二變相生之法，六曰十二律正變、倍半之法，七曰旋宮八十四聲、六十調之圖。

translations.literal: "Bell Pitches" divides front-back chapters; its front chapter has items totaling seven: first, twelve pitches yin-yang, branch-positions mutual-generation sequence chart; second, twelve pitches inch, fen, li, hao, si, hu numbers; third, five tones five phases images, clear-murky high-low order; fourth, five tones mutual-generation, diminish-increase, before-after order; fifth, altered-gong altered-zhi two alterations mutual-generation method; sixth, twelve pitches standard-alteration, double-half method; seventh, rotating-gong eighty-four tones, sixty modes chart.
translations.idiomatic: "Bell Pitches" is divided into two parts. The first part comprises seven sections: (1) a chart of the yin and yang of the twelve pitches, their branch positions, and the order of mutual generation; (2) the numbers of the twelve pitches in inches, fen, li, hao, si, and hu; (3) the images of the five tones within the five phases and the order of clear, murky, high, and low; (4) the order of mutual generation, diminishment and increase, and precedence among the five tones; (5) the method by which altered gong and altered zhi—the two alterations—generate one another; (6) the methods of standard and altered pitches and of doubling and halving; (7) a chart of the eighty-four tones of rotating gong and the sixty modes.

sentences.zh: 其後篇為條凡六：一曰明五聲之義，二曰明十二律之義，三曰律寸舊法，四曰律寸新法，五曰黃鍾分寸數法，六曰黃鍾生十一律數。

translations.literal: Its back chapter has items totaling six: first, clarify five tones' meaning; second, clarify twelve pitches' meaning; third, pitch-inch old method; fourth, pitch-inch new method; fifth, Yellow Bell fen-cun counting method; sixth, Yellow Bell generates eleven pitches' numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The second part comprises six sections: (1) explaining the meaning of the five tones; (2) explaining the meaning of the twelve pitches; (3) the old method of pitch inches; (4) the new method of pitch inches; (5) the method of counting Yellow Bell in fen and cun; (6) the numbers by which Yellow Bell generates the eleven other pitches.

sentences.zh: 大率采元定所著，更互演繹，尤為明邃。

translations.literal: generally adopting Yuan Ding's compositions, further interweaving and unfolding—especially clear and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part it draws on what Cai Yuanding wrote and develops it further through mutual elaboration, achieving a clarity and depth that is especially penetrating.

sentences.zh: 其《樂製》彙於王朝禮，其《樂舞》彙於祭禮，上下千載，旁搜遠紹，昭示前聖禮樂之非迂，而將期古樂之復見於今，熹蓋深致意焉。

translations.literal: Its "Music Institutions" collected in court-royal rites; its "Music Dance" collected in sacrifice rites—up-down a thousand years, searching widely transmitting far, displaying former sages' ritual-music not abstruse, yet hoping ancient music again appears today; Xi surely deeply intended this.
translations.idiomatic: "Music Institutions" is gathered under the rites of the royal court, and "Music Dance" under the rites of sacrifice. Spanning a thousand years, searching widely and transmitting from afar, it shows that the ritual music of the former sages was not impractical, and looks forward to ancient music appearing again in the present—toward which Xi surely directed his deepest intent.

sentences.zh: 其《詩樂篇》別係於後。

translations.literal: Its "Ode Music" chapter is separately attached afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter "Ode Music" is appended separately at the end.
